title.en: Volume 418 Biographies 205: Yuan Jiasan son: Bao Heng, Mao Changxi
title.raw: 卷418 列傳二百五 袁甲三子：保恒 毛昶熙

sentences.zh: 列傳二百五

translations.literal: Biographies 205
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 205

sentences.zh: 袁甲三子保恆毛昶熙

translations.literal: Yuan Jiasan; his sons Bao Heng and Mao Changxi
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiasan; his sons Bao Heng and Mao Changxi

sentences.zh: 袁甲三，字午橋，河南項城人。

translations.literal: Yuan Jiasan, style name Wuqiao, was a native of Xiangcheng in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Jiasan, whose style was Wuqiao, came from Xiangcheng in Henan.

sentences.zh: 道光十五年進士，授禮部主事，充軍機章京，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year of Daoguang he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, served as a clerk in the Grand Council, and was promoted in succession to bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: He became a jinshi in the fifteenth year of the Daoguang reign, received appointment as a principal secretary in the Ministry of Rites, served on the Grand Council staff, and rose step by step to bureau director.

sentences.zh: 三十年，遷御史、給事中，疏劾廣西巡撫鄭祖琛慈柔釀亂，又劾江西巡撫陳阡賄賂交通，皆罷之。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was transferred to censor and supervising secretary; he memorialized impeaching Guangxi governor Zheng Zuchen for indulgent softness that bred rebellion, and also impeaching Jiangxi governor Chen Qian for bribery and illicit connections; both were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was moved to the posts of censor and supervising secretary. He submitted memorials impeaching Guangxi governor Zheng Zuchen for being so indulgent that he invited rebellion, and Jiangxi governor Chen Qian for bribery and back-channel dealings; both men were removed from office.

sentences.zh: 戶部复捐例，疏請收回成命。

translations.literal: When the Ministry of Revenue revived the sale of offices, he memorialized asking that the imperial decision be withdrawn.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ministry of Revenue revived the sale of offices, he memorialized asking the throne to rescind the order.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，粵匪起，南河豐北決口，上疏極論時事，皆切中利弊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng the Cantonese rebels rose, and the Fengbei breach opened on the South River; he submitted memorials discussing current affairs at length, all striking to the heart of advantage and harm.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianfeng, as the Taiping rebellion broke out and the Fengbei dike burst on the South River, he submitted lengthy memorials on current affairs, each hitting the mark on what would help or harm the state.

sentences.zh: 二年，粵匪竄湖南，疏言：「總督程矞採為守土之臣，責無旁貸。

translations.literal: In the second year the Cantonese rebels fled into Hunan; he memorialized saying: "Governor-general Cheng Yucai, as the official charged with guarding the territory, bears responsibility that admits no evasion.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, when the rebels pushed into Hunan, he wrote: "Governor-general Cheng Yucai, as the official charged with defending the province, bears responsibility that cannot be shifted elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 若復令賽尚阿持節移軍，誠恐諉過爭功，互相掣肘。

translations.literal: If Sai Shanga is again ordered to take the imperial insignia and shift the army, I truly fear they will shirk blame and vie for merit, each restraining the other.
translations.idiomatic: If Sai Shanga is again sent with imperial authority to take over the campaign, I fear they will only trade blame, compete for credit, and tie each other's hands.

sentences.zh: 請命賽尚阿回京，專責程矞採便宜行事，如有疏虞，按律定罪。

translations.literal: I ask that Sai Shanga be ordered back to the capital, and that Cheng Yucai alone be charged to act as circumstances require; if there is negligence, let him be punished according to law.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that Sai Shanga be recalled to the capital and Cheng Yucai alone be empowered to act as circumstances require; if he fails, let him be punished under the law.

sentences.zh: 」並言：「湖北巡撫龔裕聞賊入境，託疾乞休，尤宜嚴懲，以昭炯戒。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Hubei governor Gong Yu, on hearing that bandits had entered the province, pleaded illness and asked to retire; he especially ought to be sternly punished, to make a clear warning.
translations.idiomatic: " He added: "When Hubei governor Gong Yu heard that rebels had entered his province, he pleaded illness and asked to retire; he above all deserves severe punishment, to set a clear example.

sentences.zh: 」又列款奏劾定郡王載銓賣弄橫勢，擅作威福，及刑部侍郎書元貪鄙險詐，諂事載銓狀，詔詰載銓所收門生實據，疏請飭呈出所繪息肩圖，事皆得實。

translations.literal: " He also listed charges memorializing impeachment of Prince Ding Zaiquan for flaunting overbearing power and arrogating authority and favor, and of Vice Minister of Justice Shu Yuan for greed, baseness, craft, and deceit, and the manner in which he fawned on Zaiquan; an edict questioned Zaiquan for factual evidence on the disciples he had taken, and a memorial asked that he be ordered to produce the "Shoulder-Relieving" painting he had commissioned; the matters were all verified.
translations.idiomatic: " He also laid out charges against Prince Ding, Zaiquan, for throwing his weight around and acting as if favor were his to grant, and against Vice Minister of Justice Shu Yuan for greed, meanness, and sycophancy toward Zaiquan. The court demanded proof of the disciples Zaiquan had taken, and Yuan asked that he be ordered to produce the "Shoulder-Relieving" picture he had commissioned; every allegation was borne out.

sentences.zh: 載銓坐罰王俸，奪領侍衛大臣兼官，書元及尚書恆春降調，題圖者降謫罰俸有差。

translations.literal: Zaiquan was penalized by forfeiture of princely stipend and stripped of his concurrent post as commanding imperial guardsman; Shu Yuan and Minister Hengchun were demoted and transferred; those who had inscribed the painting were demoted, banished, and fined stipend in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Zaiquan was fined his princely stipend and stripped of his concurrent post commanding the imperial guard; Shu Yuan and Minister Hengchun were demoted and transferred; those who had inscribed the painting received varying penalties of demotion, exile, and forfeiture of salary.

sentences.zh: 於是直聲震中外。

translations.literal: Thereupon his reputation for blunt integrity shook the court and the realm.
translations.idiomatic: From then on his reputation for fearless integrity resounded at court and abroad.

sentences.zh: 三年，命赴安徽佐侍郎呂賢基軍務。

translations.literal: In the third year he was ordered to go to Anhui to assist Vice Minister Lü Xianji in military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was ordered to Anhui to assist Vice Minister Lü Xianji with military affairs.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陷鳳陽府，踞明淮關，煽動土匪，連陷蒙城、懷遠。

translations.literal: The Cantonese rebels took Fengyang Prefecture, occupied Minghuaiguan, stirred up local bandits, and in succession captured Mengcheng and Huaiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels seized Fengyang Prefecture, held Minghuaiguan, stirred up local bandits, and in quick succession overran Mengcheng and Huaiyuan.

sentences.zh: 甲三至軍，疏言：「賊勢未遽北犯，請飭諸臣勿涉張皇，急圖制賊。

translations.literal: When Jiasan reached the army, he memorialized saying: "The bandits' strength will not immediately invade northward; I ask that the various officials be admonished not to indulge alarm, and that suppressing the bandits be urgently planned.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiasan joined the army, he wrote: "The rebels are not about to drive north at once; I ask that officials be warned against panic and urged to focus on defeating them.

sentences.zh: 」命權廬鳳道。

translations.literal: " He was ordered to act as Luzhou-Fengyang circuit intendant.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed acting Luzhou-Fengyang circuit intendant.

sentences.zh: 漢、回相閧，圍潁州，遣兵解散，誅首亂，事即定。

translations.literal: Han and Hui were in mutual strife and besieged Yingzhou; he sent troops to disperse them, executed the ringleaders, and the affair was immediately settled.
translations.idiomatic: When Han and Hui communities clashed and besieged Yingzhou, he sent troops to break up the fighting, executed the ringleaders, and the disturbance was quickly ended.

sentences.zh: 會漕運總督週天爵卒於亳州，命代領其軍。

translations.literal: It happened that Grain Transport governor Zhou Tianjue died at Bozhou; he was ordered to take command of his army in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: When Grain Transport governor Zhou Tianjue died at Bozhou, Jiasan was ordered to take over his forces.

sentences.zh: 時土匪合五十八捻為一，勢甚張。

translations.literal: At the time local bandits united fifty-eight Nian groups into one, and their power was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Local bandits had meanwhile united fifty-eight Nian factions into one force, and their power was formidable.

sentences.zh: 甲三至王市集，收散勇，整民團，擊賊高公廟，破之，加三品卿銜。

translations.literal: Jiasan reached Wangji Market, gathered scattered braves, organized civilian militia, attacked the bandits at Gaogong Temple, defeated them, and was given the honorary rank of third-grade court official.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan reached Wangji Market, rallied scattered fighters, organized militia, attacked the rebels at Gaogong Temple, routed them, and was granted the honorary rank of third-grade court official.

sentences.zh: 命署布政使，疏辭不赴，請專治兵事，允之；

translations.literal: He was ordered to act as provincial treasurer; he memorialized declining and not going, asking to devote himself solely to military affairs; this was granted;
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed acting provincial treasurer, but memorialized that he would not take up civil duties and asked to concentrate on military affairs; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 命專剿捻匪，破賊標裡鋪，擒其渠鄧大俊。

translations.literal: he was ordered to devote himself to suppressing the Nian bandits, broke the bandits at Biaoli Shop, and captured their chieftain Deng Dajun.
translations.idiomatic: He was then ordered to focus on suppressing the Nian rebels, smashed them at Biaoli Shop, and captured their leader Deng Dajun.

sentences.zh: 鄉團先後擒獻者二千餘，悉置之法。

translations.literal: Militia who in succession captured and presented more than two thousand were all executed according to law.
translations.idiomatic: More than two thousand captives whom militia had turned in over time were all put to death.

sentences.zh: 十月，粵匪由安慶竄踞桐城，尋陷舒城，呂賢基死之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the Cantonese rebels from Anqing fled and occupied Tongcheng, soon after took Shucheng, and Lü Xianji died in the fighting.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the rebels broke out from Anqing and seized Tongcheng; they soon took Shucheng as well, and Lü Xianji was killed.

sentences.zh: 上命移軍桐城，甲三疏言：「捻首張茂踞懷、蒙間，窺廬郡，請先赴蒙、亳為諸郡聲援。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the army shifted to Tongcheng; Jiasan memorialized saying: "The Nian chieftain Zhang Mao occupies the ground between Huaiyuan and Mengcheng and watches Luzhou Prefecture; I ask first to go to Mengcheng and Bozhou as a supporting force for the various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered the army moved to Tongcheng, but Jiasan wrote: "Nian leader Zhang Mao holds the ground between Huaiyuan and Mengcheng and is eyeing Luzhou; I ask to go first to Mengcheng and Bozhou to support the surrounding prefectures.

sentences.zh: 」時捻匪麕聚雉河集，甲三令縣丞徐曉峰擊破之，擒賊渠孫重倫。

translations.literal: " At the time Nian bandits were densely gathered at Zhiheji; Jiasan ordered subprefect Xu Xiaofeng to attack and break them, capturing the bandit chieftain Sun Chonglun.
translations.idiomatic: " The Nian were massed at Zhiheji; Jiasan had subprefect Xu Xiaofeng break them up and capture their leader Sun Chonglun.

sentences.zh: 分兵擊敗臨湖鋪竄匪，擒賊渠宮步雲、馬九，併其目數十人。

translations.literal: He divided troops to attack and defeat fleeing bandits at Linhu Shop, capturing the bandit chieftains Gong Buyun and Ma Jiu, together with several dozen of their lieutenants.
translations.idiomatic: He sent detachments to defeat rebels who had fled to Linhu Shop, capturing leaders Gong Buyun and Ma Jiu along with several dozen of their officers.

sentences.zh: 令游擊錢朝舉、知縣米鎮攻懷遠，大破之，張茂負傷遁。

translations.literal: He ordered brigade commander Qian Chaoju and magistrate Mi Zhen to attack Huaiyuan, inflicted a great defeat, and Zhang Mao fled wounded.
translations.idiomatic: He had brigade commander Qian Chaoju and magistrate Mi Zhen attack Huaiyuan, inflicted a crushing defeat, and Zhang Mao escaped wounded.

sentences.zh: 十二月，賊陷廬州，巡撫江忠源戰歿。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month the bandits took Luzhou; governor Jiang Zhongyuan died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month the rebels took Luzhou, and governor Jiang Zhongyuan was killed in battle.

sentences.zh: 甲三劾陝甘總督舒興阿擁兵坐視，褫其職；

translations.literal: Jiasan impeached Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general Shu Xing'a for holding troops and sitting by watching, and stripped him of office;
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan impeached Shaanxi-Gansu governor-general Shu Xing'a for holding his troops back while looking on, and had him dismissed;

sentences.zh: 並請撥兵防壽卅、六安以杜旁擾。

translations.literal: and also asked that troops be detached to guard Shouzhou and Lu'an to cut off side harassment.
translations.idiomatic: he also asked that troops be sent to guard Shouzhou and Lu'an and block flanking raids.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，粵匪陷六安，竄蒙城，甲三進搗蒙城。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year the Cantonese rebels took Lu'an and fled into Mengcheng; Jiasan advanced to strike at Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year the rebels took Lu'an and fled into Mengcheng; Jiasan advanced against Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 賊走永城，甲三恐其趨宿、徐，阻糧道，急躡之，賊已濟河，不及而還。

translations.literal: The bandits fled to Yongcheng; Jiasan feared they would rush toward Suzhou and Xuzhou and block the grain route, pursued them urgently, but the bandits had already crossed the river and he returned without overtaking them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled to Yongcheng; fearing they would strike toward Suzhou and Xuzhou and cut the grain route, Jiasan pursued hard, but they had already crossed the river and he had to turn back.

sentences.zh: 賊尋复南竄，連敗之潁州、正陽關，餘賊退六安。

translations.literal: The bandits soon again fled south; he defeated them in succession at Yingzhou and Zhengyangguan, and the remnant bandits withdrew to Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels soon turned south again; he defeated them in succession at Yingzhou and Zhengyangguan, and the survivors fell back on Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 還軍蒙、亳剿捻匪，搗臨湖鋪，進偪雉河集。

translations.literal: He returned the army to Mengcheng and Bozhou to suppress Nian bandits, struck Linhu Shop, and advanced pressing on Zhiheji.
translations.idiomatic: He brought his army back to Mengcheng and Bozhou to fight the Nian, hit Linhu Shop, and pressed toward Zhiheji.

sentences.zh: 賊空巢誘官軍，甲三偵知，盡泊船南岸，令知州張家駒陣河干，參將硃連泰、李成虎敗賊馬家樓，迫之渦河，殲賊殆盡，遂破義門集，捻首張捷三遁去。

translations.literal: The bandits emptied their nest to lure the government army; Jiasan learned this by reconnaissance, moored all boats on the south bank, ordered prefect Zhang Jiaju to form battle line on the river bank, and had brigade generals Zhu Liantai and Li Chenghu defeat the bandits at Majialou, pressed them to the Wo River, and annihilated the bandits nearly to the last man; he then broke Yimenji, and the Nian chieftain Zhang Jiesan fled away.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels emptied their base to lure government troops; Jiasan learned of the ruse, anchored every boat on the south bank, posted prefect Zhang Jiaju along the river, and had brigade generals Zhu Liantai and Li Chenghu rout them at Majialou, drive them to the Wo River, and wipe out nearly the whole force. He then took Yimenji while Nian leader Zhang Jiesan escaped.

sentences.zh: 甲三移屯臨淮，地數被兵，比戶凋敝。

translations.literal: Jiasan shifted camp to Linhuai; the region had repeatedly suffered warfare, and household after household was depleted.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan moved his headquarters to Linhuai, a district repeatedly ravaged by war where household after household lay in ruin.

sentences.zh: 既至，討軍實，撫殘黎，眾皆樂為之用，超擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: Once he arrived, he reviewed the true state of the army, comforted the surviving populace, and all were glad to serve him; he was promoted by exception to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he inspected the army's real strength, comforted the survivors, and won men so willingly that he was promoted out of turn to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「皖軍以克復廬州為急，宜出偏師赴南路斷賊接濟。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "The Anhui army should make recovering Luzhou urgent; a detached force ought to be sent to the southern route to cut off the bandits' supplies.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote: "The Anhui forces should make retaking Luzhou their first priority and send a flank column south to cut rebel supply lines.

sentences.zh: 」尋以賊陷和州，窺江浦，將北竄。

translations.literal: " Soon after, because the bandits took Hezhou, watched Jiangpu, and were about to flee northward,
translations.idiomatic: " Soon afterward the rebels took Hezhou, threatened Jiangpu, and seemed ready to drive north.

sentences.zh: 分遣將扼關山，赴滁河鳩團練為聲援。

translations.literal: he sent generals in detachments to hold Guanshan and went to Chuzhou to rally militia as a supporting force.
translations.idiomatic: He sent generals to hold Guanshan and went to Chuzhou to rally militia as reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 十月，北路捻匪复熾，令張家駒、硃連泰率軍破之於寺覺集。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the northern-route Nian bandits again flared up; he ordered Zhang Jiaju and Zhu Liantai to lead the army and defeat them at Sijueji.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the northern Nian flared up again; he had Zhang Jiaju and Zhu Liantai defeat them at Sijueji.

sentences.zh: 粵匪踞烏江，令廬鳳道張吉第擊敗之。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebels occupied Wujiang; he ordered Luzhou-Fengyang circuit intendant Zhang Jidi to attack and defeat them.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping forces held Wujiang; he had Luzhou-Fengyang intendant Zhang Jidi drive them off.

sentences.zh: 賊夜結五壘於駐馬河，乘其初至薄之，殲擒甚眾。

translations.literal: The bandits by night linked five forts at Zhuma River; he took advantage of their first arrival to press them closely, killing and capturing a great host.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels built five camps overnight at Zhuma River; he struck while they were still settling in and killed or captured a great number.

sentences.zh: 令參將劉玉豹、舉人臧紆青規桐城，連奪大小關，擊走廬江援賊。

translations.literal: He ordered brigade general Liu Yubao and juren Zang Yuqing to plan against Tongcheng, in succession seized large and small passes, and drove off Luzhou-Jiang reinforcements for the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He had brigade general Liu Yubao and juren Zang Yuqing press Tongcheng, seize pass after pass, and beat back rebel reinforcements from Lujiang.

sentences.zh: 紆青戰甚銳，進攻桐城西門，賊由安慶、潛山來援，城賊出應之，紆青戰死，玉豹收餘眾退保六安。

translations.literal: Yuqing fought very sharply, advanced to attack Tongcheng's west gate; bandits came to reinforce from Anqing and Qianshan, the city bandits sallied to meet them, Yuqing died in battle, and Yubao gathered the remnant troops and withdrew to hold Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: Yuqing fought fiercely and assaulted Tongcheng's west gate, but rebels came up from Anqing and Qianshan and the garrison sallied to meet them; Yuqing was killed, and Yubao gathered the survivors and fell back to defend Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 五年，疏陳軍事，略曰：「北路以臨淮為要，正陽次之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he memorialized setting forth military affairs, in summary saying: "On the northern route Linhuai is essential, Zhengyang next.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he laid out the military situation in a memorial, writing in part: "On the northern front Linhuai is the key point and Zhengyang the next.

sentences.zh: 臣駐臨淮，牛鑑扼正陽，以防賊北渡。

translations.literal: Your servant is stationed at Linhuai, Niu Jian holds Zhengyang, to guard against the bandits crossing north.
translations.idiomatic: I am posted at Linhuai and Niu Jian at Zhengyang to keep the rebels from crossing north.

sentences.zh: 廬州為中路，和春、福濟師老力疲，久攻不下。

translations.literal: Luzhou is the central route; Hechun and Fuji's armies are aged and weary in strength, and have long attacked without taking it.
translations.idiomatic: Luzhou is the central front, but Hechun and Fuji's armies are worn out and have failed for months to take the city.

sentences.zh: 西路蘄、黃無處非賊，兵力過單。

translations.literal: On the western route Qichun and Huangzhou have bandits everywhere; military strength is too thin.
translations.idiomatic: On the west, Qichun and Huangzhou are overrun, and our forces there are far too few.

sentences.zh: 東路沿江針魚嘴、西梁山，賊船賊壘，來去無常。

translations.literal: On the eastern route along the river at Zhenyu Mouth and Xiliang Hill are bandit boats and bandit forts, coming and going without constancy.
translations.idiomatic: Along the eastern Yangtze at Zhenyu Mouth and Xiliang Hill rebel boats and camps appear and vanish without pattern.

sentences.zh: 張光第等分軍進攻，然無水師夾擊，終難收效。

translations.literal: Zhang Guangdi and others divided the army to advance and attack, yet without a naval force to strike from both sides, in the end it is hard to gain effect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Guangdi and others have attacked in detachments, but without a naval force to strike from the river, little can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 目下悍賊力爭江路，群聚上游，廬州有機可乘，請益厚兵力，分扼廬城東南，或增兵並剿舒、巢，俾其應接不暇，庶可一鼓而下。

translations.literal: At present fierce bandits are striving for the river route and massing upstream; Luzhou has an opening that may be seized; I ask to thicken military strength, divide forces to hold Luzhou city's southeast, or increase troops to jointly suppress Shucheng and Chaohu, so that they cannot answer calls in time, and then perhaps it may be taken in one drumbeat.
translations.idiomatic: The main rebel force is now fighting for control of the river and massing upstream, while Luzhou may be vulnerable. I ask for heavier forces to block the city's southeast, or added troops to strike Shucheng and Chaohu at once so the enemy cannot respond everywhere; then Luzhou might fall in a single assault.

sentences.zh: 時淮北官吏，甲三欲有更調，和春、福濟意不合，甲三專奏，詔仍飭會銜。

translations.literal: At the time regarding officials north of the Huai, Jiasan wished to make transfers and replacements; Hechun and Fuji were not of one mind; Jiasan memorialized separately, and an edict still ordered joint signature.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan wanted to reshuffle officials north of the Huai, but Hechun and Fuji disagreed; when he memorialized on his own, the court still ordered joint signature with them.

sentences.zh: 於是和春、福濟疏劾甲三堅執己見，並劾其株守臨淮，粉飾軍情，擅裁餉銀，冒銷肥己。

translations.literal: Thereupon Hechun and Fuji memorialized impeaching Jiasan for stubbornly holding to his own views, and also impeaching him for clinging to Linhuai, embellishing military reports, arbitrarily cutting rations and silver, and falsely expending funds to enrich himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hechun and Fuji then impeached him for stubbornness, for staying put at Linhuai while glossing over the war situation, for cutting rations on his own authority, and for padding expenses to enrich himself.

sentences.zh: 召回京，部議褫職。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital; the ministry deliberated stripping his office.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital, and the ministries recommended dismissal.

sentences.zh: 甲三呈訴被誣，下兩江總督按治，事得白。

translations.literal: Jiasan submitted a plea that he had been slandered; the case was sent down to the Liangjiang governor-general for investigation, and the matter was cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan protested that he had been slandered; the Liangjiang governor-general investigated, and he was cleared.

sentences.zh: 甲三在淮北得軍民心，其去也，軍民泣留者塞道。

translations.literal: Jiasan in northern Huai had won the hearts of army and people; when he left, soldiers and civilians weeping and begging him to stay blocked the road.
translations.idiomatic: He had won the loyalty of soldiers and civilians north of the Huai, and when he left, weeping crowds begging him to stay filled the roads.

sentences.zh: 未幾，捻首張洛行勾結皖、豫諸捻，勢益熾。

translations.literal: Before long Nian chieftain Zhang Luoxing linked with the various Nian of Anhui and Henan, and their power grew fiercer.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Nian leader Zhang Luoxing united factions across Anhui and Henan, and the rebellion burned hotter.

sentences.zh: 懷遠民胡文忠鬻子女，徒步京師，控都察院求以甲三回鎮，格不達，懷狀自縊。

translations.literal: Huaiyuan commoner Hu Wenzhong sold his sons and daughters, walked on foot to the capital, lodged a complaint at the Censorate asking that Jiasan be sent back to his post, was blocked from reaching the throne, and hanged himself clutching his petition.
translations.idiomatic: A Huaiyuan man named Hu Wenzhong sold his children, walked to the capital, and petitioned the Censorate to send Jiasan back; when the petition never reached the throne, he hanged himself clutching the document.

sentences.zh: 言官孫觀、曹登庸、宗稷辰先後疏請起用；

translations.literal: Censorial officials Sun Guan, Cao Dengyong, and Zong Jichen in succession memorialized asking that he be re-employed;
translations.idiomatic: Censors Sun Guan, Cao Dengyong, and Zong Jichen memorialized one after another asking that he be reappointed;

sentences.zh: 疆臣怡良、吉爾杭阿、何桂清亦交章論薦。

translations.literal: frontier officials Yiliang, Jierhang'a, and He Guiqing also submitted memorials in turn recommending him.
translations.idiomatic: and frontier governors Yiliang, Jierhang'a, and He Guiqing also wrote in his favor.

sentences.zh: 六年二月，命隨同英桂剿捻河南。

translations.literal: In the second month of the sixth year he was ordered to accompany Ying Gui in suppressing the Nian in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the sixth year he was ordered to join Ying Gui in suppressing the Nian in Henan.

sentences.zh: 甲三赴歸德，招集舊部，三戰三捷，進解亳州之圍，毀白龍王廟砦，破燕家小樓賊數万，直搗雉河集，擒蘇天福，洛行僅身免，特詔嘉獎，命以三品京堂候補。

translations.literal: Jiasan went to Guide, gathered his old subordinates, three battles and three victories, advanced to relieve the siege of Bozhou, destroyed the White Dragon King Temple stockade, broke tens of thousands of bandits at Yan Family Small Tower, drove straight to strike Zhiheji, captured Su Tianfu, Luoxing barely escaped with his body, received a special edict of praise, and was ordered to await appointment as capital official of third grade.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan went to Guide, rallied his old troops, and won three battles in a row. He relieved the siege of Bozhou, destroyed the White Dragon King Temple stockade, smashed tens of thousands of rebels at Yan Family Small Tower, and drove straight to Zhiheji, capturing Su Tianfu while Luoxing barely escaped. The court issued a special commendation and named him a third-grade capital official awaiting appointment.

sentences.zh: 洛行尋复糾黨犯潁州，擊走之，又踞雉河集。

translations.literal: Luoxing soon again gathered followers and invaded Yingzhou; Jiasan attacked and drove them off, but they again occupied Zhiheji.
translations.idiomatic: Luoxing soon rallied his men and struck Yingzhou; Jiasan beat him back, but the Nian seized Zhiheji again.

sentences.zh: 七年，平王、鄧、宋、姚諸圩，誅捻渠李寅等百餘人，授太僕寺卿，賜花翎。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he pacified the Wang, Deng, Song, and Yao stockades, executed more than a hundred Nian chieftains including Li Yin, was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud, and was granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he pacified the Wang, Deng, Song, and Yao stockades, executed more than a hundred Nian leaders including Li Yin, was appointed Grand Minister of the Imperial Stud, and received the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 勝保督師攻張洛行於正陽關，久不下，奏請甲三合剿，令部將硃連泰、史榮椿攻韓圩，克之。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao supervised the army attacking Zhang Luoxing at Zhengyangguan and for a long time could not take it; he memorialized asking Jiasan to join in suppression, and ordered subordinate generals Zhu Liantai and Shi Rongchun to attack Han Stockade and capture it.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao had long besieged Zhang Luoxing at Zhengyangguan without success and asked Jiasan to join the campaign; Jiasan had Zhu Liantai and Shi Rongchun take Han Stockade.

sentences.zh: 八年，偕勝保解固始之圍，复六安。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, together with Sheng Bao, he relieved the siege of Gushi and recovered Lu'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he and Sheng Bao lifted the siege of Gushi and retook Lu'an.

sentences.zh: 史榮椿破捻匪於銅山，斬其渠孫大旺。

translations.literal: Shi Rongchun defeated Nian bandits at Tongshan and beheaded their chieftain Sun Dawang.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Rongchun defeated the Nian at Tongshan and beheaded their leader Sun Dawang.

sentences.zh: 移軍宿州，襲賊王家圩，誅賊首王紹堂等，乘勝复七圩。

translations.literal: He shifted the army to Suzhou, raided the bandits at Wang Family Stockade, executed the bandit leaders Wang Shaotang and others, and riding the victory recovered seven stockades.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Suzhou, raided Wang Family Stockade, executed leaders including Wang Shaotang, and in the same momentum retook seven stockades.

sentences.zh: 七月，命代勝保督辦三省剿匪事宜。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he was ordered to replace Sheng Bao in supervising the three provinces' bandit-suppression affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he was ordered to replace Sheng Bao as supervisor of bandit suppression across three provinces.

sentences.zh: 張洛行方踞陳家莊，擊走之，分兵复豐縣。

translations.literal: Zhang Luoxing was just then occupying Chen Family Village; Jiasan attacked and drove him off, and divided troops to recover Feng County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Luoxing was holding Chen Family Village; Jiasan drove him off and sent detachments to retake Feng County.

sentences.zh: 未幾，蒙、亳諸捻入歸德，窺周家口，甲三令子保恆偕總兵傅振邦馳援。

translations.literal: Before long the Mengcheng, Bozhou, and other Nian entered Guide and watched Zhoujiakou; Jiasan ordered his son Bao Heng together with regional commander Fu Zhenbang to hurry to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Nian from Mengcheng and Bozhou entered Guide and threatened Zhoujiakou; Jiasan sent his son Bao Heng with regional commander Fu Zhenbang to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 賊遽趨西北，偪開封，振邦追賊，及之太和李興集。

translations.literal: The bandits suddenly rushed northwest, pressing on Kaifeng; Zhenbang pursued the bandits and caught them at Taihe Li Xingji.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels suddenly veered northwest toward Kaifeng; Zhenbang pursued and caught them at Taihe Li Xingji.

sentences.zh: 保恆集團勇扼橋口，馬步合擊，大破之，殲斃數千，逐賊出河南境，賜號伊勒圖巴圖魯。

translations.literal: Bao Heng gathered militia to hold Qiaokou; cavalry and infantry joined in attack and inflicted a great defeat, killing several thousand, pursued the bandits out of Henan territory, and was granted the title Yiletu Batulu.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Heng rallied militia at Qiaokou; cavalry and infantry struck together, inflicted a crushing defeat, killed several thousand, and drove the rebels out of Henan. He was granted the title Yiletu Baturu.

sentences.zh: 疏言：「兵分則勢孤，合則勢盛。

translations.literal: He memorialized saying: "When troops are divided the force is isolated; when united the force is strong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan wrote: "Divided armies grow weak; united armies grow strong.

sentences.zh: 捻匪踞地千餘裡，臣兵不過數千，不能制賊死命。

translations.literal: The Nian bandits occupy more than a thousand li of ground; your servant's troops are no more than several thousand and cannot control the bandits' lives unto death.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian hold more than a thousand li of territory, while I have only a few thousand men and cannot destroy them outright.

sentences.zh: 請敕各督撫合力大舉，為掃穴擒渠之計。

translations.literal: I ask that an edict order all governors and governors-general to join forces in a great campaign, as a plan to sweep the nest and capture the chieftains.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that every governor and governor-general be ordered to combine forces in one great campaign to root out their nests and seize their leaders.

sentences.zh: 九年正月，擊張洛行於草溝，破其巢，追至沱河，多溺水死，复擊之雙渡口，洛行泅水免。

translations.literal: In the first month of the ninth year he attacked Zhang Luoxing at Caogou, broke his nest, pursued to the Tuo River where many drowned and died, again attacked at Shuangdukou, and Luoxing swam away and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the ninth year he attacked Zhang Luoxing at Caogou, destroyed his base, pursued him to the Tuo River where many rebels drowned, struck again at Shuangdukou, and Luoxing swam away and escaped.

sentences.zh: 勝保與甲三意不合，屢疏詆之，詔斥「甲三督剿半載，但防徐、宿，不搗賊巢，日久無效」。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao and Jiasan were not of one mind; he repeatedly memorialized slandering him; an edict rebuked: "Jiasan has supervised suppression for half a year, but only guards Xuzhou and Suzhou, does not strike the bandits' nest, and over time has no effect."
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao clashed with Jiasan and repeatedly denounced him in memorials. An edict rebuked Jiasan: "For half a year you have only guarded Xuzhou and Suzhou without striking the rebels' base, and nothing has been achieved."

sentences.zh: 召回京，入覲，面陳軍事。

translations.literal: He was recalled to the capital, entered audience, and stated military affairs to the emperor's face.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital, received audience, and presented the military situation in person.

sentences.zh: 四月，命署漕運總督。

translations.literal: In the fourth month he was ordered to act as Grain Transport governor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he was appointed acting Grain Transport governor.

sentences.zh: 尋勝保以母憂歸，命署欽差大臣，督辦安徽軍務，實授漕運總督。

translations.literal: Soon Sheng Bao returned home on account of his mother's mourning; he was ordered to act as imperial commissioner and supervise Anhui military affairs, and was substantively appointed Grain Transport governor.
translations.idiomatic: When Sheng Bao left for mourning, Jiasan was named acting imperial commissioner to supervise Anhui military affairs and was confirmed as Grain Transport governor.

sentences.zh: 進攻臨淮關，軍南岸，斷其糧道，降捻內應，斬關而入，生擒賊首顧大隴等，遂克之。

translations.literal: He advanced to attack Linhuaiguan, encamped on the south bank, cut off its grain route, had surrendering Nian act as inside collaborators, cut through the pass and entered, captured alive the bandit chieftains Gu Dalong and others, and then took it.
translations.idiomatic: He advanced on Linhuaiguan, camped on the south bank, cut rebel supply lines, used surrendering Nian as inside collaborators, broke through the pass, captured leaders including Gu Dalong alive, and took the town.

sentences.zh: 十年，進規鳳陽，屢戰皆捷。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he advanced to plan against Fengyang and in repeated battles was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he pressed Fengyang and won battle after battle.

sentences.zh: 鄧正明以府城乞降，張元隆猶據縣城，誘出誅之，並誅悍賊三百餘人。

translations.literal: Deng Zhengming begged surrender with the prefectural city; Zhang Yuanlong still held the county city; Jiasan lured him out and executed him, and also executed more than three hundred fierce bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Deng Zhengming offered to surrender the prefectural city, but Zhang Yuanlong still held the county seat; Jiasan lured him out and executed him along with more than three hundred hardened rebels.

sentences.zh: 未匝月，拔兩城，詔嘉調度有方，賜黃馬褂，命其子保恆赴軍差遣。

translations.literal: In less than a full month he took both cities; an edict praised his command as well ordered, granted the yellow riding jacket, and ordered his son Bao Heng to go to the army for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: Within a month he had taken both cities. The court praised his command, granted him the yellow riding jacket, and ordered his son Bao Heng to join the army on active duty.

sentences.zh: 捻匪陷清江浦，窺淮安，令道員張學醇擊走之，乘勝復全椒。

translations.literal: Nian bandits took Qingjiangpu and watched Huai'an; he ordered circuit intendant Zhang Xuechun to attack and drive them off, and riding the victory recovered Quanjiao.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian took Qingjiangpu and threatened Huai'an; he had circuit intendant Zhang Xuechun drive them off and followed up by retaking Quanjiao.

sentences.zh: 粵匪陳玉成來援，分擾滁州，令李世忠夾擊走之。

translations.literal: Cantonese rebel Chen Yucheng came to reinforce, divided forces to harass Chuzhou; he ordered Li Shizhong to strike from both sides and drive them off.
translations.idiomatic: Taiping commander Chen Yucheng came to reinforce and raided Chuzhou; Jiasan had Li Shizhong attack from both sides and drive him off.

sentences.zh: 是時江北無統帥，揚州叛將薛成良擁眾剽掠，亟發舟師扼高、寶諸湖。

translations.literal: At this time north of the river there was no supreme commander; Yangzhou rebel general Xue Chengliang held a host and plundered; he urgently dispatched a naval force to hold the Gaoyou and Baoying lakes.
translations.idiomatic: North of the Yangtze there was then no supreme commander, while Yangzhou mutineer Xue Chengliang led raiders on the loose; Jiasan urgently sent a flotilla to block the lakes around Gaoyou and Baoying.

sentences.zh: 成良走依李世忠，甲三責以大義，即縛獻成良，斬之以徇。

translations.literal: Chengliang fled to rely on Li Shizhong; Jiasan charged him with the great principle of righteousness, and Li immediately bound and presented Chengliang; he was beheaded as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: Chengliang fled to Li Shizhong's camp; Jiasan appealed to duty, and Li at once bound him and handed him over; Jiasan had him beheaded as an example.

sentences.zh: 令保恆合總兵張得勝、副都統花尚阿各軍圍定遠，陳玉成糾眾來援，會合捻匪撲鳳陽，據九華諸山，連營數十里。

translations.literal: He ordered Bao Heng to unite the armies of regional commander Zhang Desheng and vice commandant Hua Shang'a to besiege Dingyuan; Chen Yucheng gathered followers to reinforce, joined with Nian bandits to strike Fengyang, occupied the Jiuhua mountains, and linked camps for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: He had Bao Heng join regional commander Zhang Desheng and vice commandant Hua Shang'a in besieging Dingyuan. Chen Yucheng rallied reinforcements, the Nian struck Fengyang together with him, and they occupied the Jiuhua hills in a chain of camps stretching for miles.

sentences.zh: 城中食且盡，甲三令參將黃國瑞潛率銳卒四百夜薄九華山，躍入壘，城上發砲應之，賊大亂，棄營走，圍乃解。

translations.literal: Food in the city was nearly exhausted; Jiasan ordered brigade general Huang Guorui secretly to lead four hundred picked soldiers by night to press close to Jiuhua Hill, leap into the fort, the city above fired cannon in response, the bandits fell into great disorder, abandoned camp and fled, and the siege was then lifted.
translations.idiomatic: As food in the city ran out, Jiasan had brigade general Huang Guorui lead four hundred picked men in a night assault on Jiuhua Hill. They leaped into the camps while the garrison fired in support; the rebels broke and fled, and the siege was lifted.

sentences.zh: 是年秋，英法聯軍入京師，車駕幸熱河，甲三請率兵入衛，詔以臨淮為南北筦鑰，止勿行。

translations.literal: That autumn the Anglo-French allied armies entered the capital; the imperial carriage went to Rehe; Jiasan asked to lead troops to enter and guard, but an edict said that Linhuai was the north-south key and forbade him to go.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn Anglo-French forces entered Beijing and the court fled to Rehe. Jiasan asked to march north with his troops, but was told Linhuai was the strategic hinge between north and south and ordered to stay.

sentences.zh: 和議定，條上四事，曰：慎採納，節糜費，精訓練，選將才，下所司議行。

translations.literal: When peace was settled, he listed four matters: be careful in accepting advice, economize wasteful expenditure, refine training, and select commanders of talent; the items were sent down to the relevant offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: After peace was made, he submitted four recommendations: weigh advice carefully, cut wasteful spending, improve training, and choose capable generals; the court referred them to the relevant offices for action.

sentences.zh: 复疏請還京，泰西諸國欲助兵討賊，甲三力陳非策，皆報聞。

translations.literal: He again memorialized asking to return to the capital; Western nations wished to assist with troops in suppressing bandits; Jiasan strongly stated this was not a good policy; all were reported received.
translations.idiomatic: He again asked to return to the capital and argued strongly against letting Western powers send troops to help suppress the rebels; the court acknowledged both memorials.

sentences.zh: 十一年，張洛行屯聚渦河北，令李世忠擊走之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year, Zhang Luoxing gathered and encamped north of the Wo River; he ordered Li Shizhong to attack and drive him away.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year Zhang Luoxing massed his forces north of the Wo River; Jiasan ordered Li Shizhong to attack and drive him off.

sentences.zh: 練總苗沛霖者，鳳臺諸生，健猾為閭里雄。

translations.literal: The militia commander Miao Peilin was a licentiate of Fengtai, vigorous and cunning, a local strongman.
translations.idiomatic: The militia commander Miao Peilin was a licentiate from Fengtai—strong, shrewd, and the dominant man in his neighborhood.

sentences.zh: 以團練功累擢川北道，加布政使銜，然不冠服，令其下稱「先生」。

translations.literal: For militia-training merit he was promoted in succession to intendant of North Sichuan circuit, with the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner, yet he wore no official cap and robe and had his subordinates call him "Sir."
translations.idiomatic: For his militia service he rose step by step to intendant of North Sichuan circuit with the nominal rank of provincial administration commissioner, yet he wore no official dress and had his men address him simply as "Sir."

sentences.zh: 所平賊圩輒置長，收其田租。

translations.literal: Wherever he pacified rebel stockades he would appoint chiefs and collect their land rents.
translations.idiomatic: In every rebel stockade he subdued he installed a headman and collected the land rent for himself.

sentences.zh: 緣道設關隘，壟斷公私。

translations.literal: Along the roads he set up passes and barriers, monopolizing public and private commerce.
translations.idiomatic: He planted checkpoints along the roads and seized control of both public and private trade.

sentences.zh: 渦河、澮、潁之間，跋扈自恣。

translations.literal: Between the Wo River, the Hui, and the Ying, he acted overbearingly and as he pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Between the Wo, Hui, and Ying rivers he lorded it over the region and did as he liked.

sentences.zh: 甲三屢羈縻之，用以牽制捻匪。

translations.literal: Jiasan repeatedly kept him on a loose rein and used him to check the Nian bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan repeatedly kept him on a loose leash, using him to tie down the Nian.

sentences.zh: 勝保尤信用沛霖，沛霖亦深與結納，內懷反側，憚威不敢猝發。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao especially trusted Peilin; Peilin also formed a deep alliance with him, yet inwardly harbored rebellious intent and, fearing his authority, did not dare act suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao trusted Peilin above all, and Peilin in turn cultivated a close bond with him; inwardly he nursed treason, but fearing Sheng Bao's power he did not dare strike at once.

sentences.zh: 至是藉口其練勇被害，據懷遠，圍壽州，巡撫翁同書為所劫持，殺壽州團練徐立壯；

translations.literal: At this point, taking as his pretext that his militiamen had been killed, he seized Huaiyuan, besieged Shouzhou, took governor Weng Tongshu hostage, and killed Shouzhou militia leader Xu Lizuang;
translations.idiomatic: At this he seized on the pretext that his militiamen had been murdered, occupied Huaiyuan, and besieged Shouzhou; he held governor Weng Tongshu hostage and killed Shouzhou militia leader Xu Lizuang;

sentences.zh: 囚孫家泰，亦自盡，而壽州之圍仍不撤；

translations.literal: He imprisoned Sun Jiatai, who also took his own life, yet the siege of Shouzhou was still not lifted;
translations.idiomatic: he imprisoned Sun Jiatai, who also killed himself, yet still did not lift the siege of Shouzhou;

sentences.zh: 遣其黨苟憬開犯河南，受粵匪封職，令練眾蓄髮，四出擾掠。

translations.literal: He sent his follower Gou Jingkai to invade Henan, accepted a Taiping commission, ordered his militia to grow their hair long, and sent them out on all sides to raid and plunder.
translations.idiomatic: he sent his follower Gou Jingkai to raid Henan, accepted a Taiping commission, ordered his militia to wear the long hair of the rebels, and sent them out in every direction to loot.

sentences.zh: 於是詔褫沛霖職，命甲三會諸軍進剿，同書罷去，賈臻代署巡撫，复於潁州被圍。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict stripped Peilin of his rank, ordered Jiasan to join the armies in a punitive campaign, removed Weng Tongshu, had Jia Zhen act as governor, and again Yingzhou was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: The court then stripped Peilin of office and ordered Jiasan to lead a joint punitive campaign; Weng Tongshu was dismissed, Jia Zhen served as acting governor, and Yingzhou came under siege again.

sentences.zh: 會張洛行大舉渡淮，甲三移軍擊之，洛行敗走。

translations.literal: Just then Zhang Luoxing crossed the Huai in force; Jiasan shifted troops to attack him, and Luoxing fled in defeat.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Luoxing crossed the Huai in force, Jiasan shifted his army to strike him and Luoxing was beaten and fled.

sentences.zh: 甲三屯長淮衛，解散沛霖屬圩二百餘處。

translations.literal: Jiasan encamped at Changhuaiwei and dissolved more than two hundred stockades under Peilin's control.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan encamped at Changhuaiwei and broke up more than two hundred stockades belonging to Peilin's followers.

sentences.zh: 十一月，保恆偕總兵張得勝等克定​​遠，粵匪遁走，進拔六合、天長。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Bao Heng together with regional commander Zhang Desheng and others took Dingyuan; the Taiping forces fled, and they advanced to recover Liuhe and Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Bao Heng joined regional commander Zhang Desheng and others in taking Dingyuan; the Taiping forces fled, and they went on to recover Liuhe and Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，會克江浦、浦口，移軍會多隆阿軍攻廬州，克之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi they jointly took Jiangpu and Pukou, moved the army to join Duolong'a's force in attacking Luzhou, and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi they took Jiangpu and Pukou, then moved to join Duolong'a in attacking Luzhou and captured the city.

sentences.zh: 陳玉成走壽州投苗沛霖，執送勝保軍，誅之。

translations.literal: Chen Yucheng fled to Shouzhou and submitted to Miao Peilin, who seized him and sent him to Sheng Bao's camp, where he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Yucheng fled to Shouzhou and sought refuge with Miao Peilin, who seized him and handed him over to Sheng Bao's army to be executed.

sentences.zh: 於是勝保為沛霖乞恩免罪，責剿捻自效，佯奉命而倔僵如故。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sheng Bao pleaded for clemency for Peilin, charged him to suppress the Nian as proof of loyalty, and Peilin feigned obedience yet remained as obstinate as before.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao then pleaded for Peilin to be spared, assigning him to suppress the Nian as proof of loyalty; Peilin pretended to obey but was as stiff-necked as ever.

sentences.zh: 甲三策沛霖終為患，疏陳大勢，先剿群捻，次沛霖。

translations.literal: Jiasan judged that Peilin would ultimately become a menace; he memorialized on the overall situation, proposing first to suppress the Nian bands collectively, then Peilin.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan concluded that Peilin would ultimately be a disaster and memorialized on the larger strategy: first crush the Nian bands together, then deal with Peilin.

sentences.zh: 薦李續宜撫皖，而自移師會僧格林沁軍擊捻匪，上報可。

translations.literal: He recommended Li Xuyi to govern Anhui, while he himself moved troops to join Senggeliqin's army in attacking the Nian; the throne approved.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Li Xuyi as governor of Anhui and moved his own forces to join Senggeliqin against the Nian; the emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 尋以病劇乞罷，允之。

translations.literal: Soon, gravely ill, he asked to be relieved of duty; the request was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Soon, gravely ill, he asked to be relieved of his post, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 前因壽州失陷，部議革職，特詔寬免。

translations.literal: Earlier, because Shouzhou had fallen, the Board had recommended stripping him of rank, but a special edict exempted him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the fall of Shouzhou, the Board had recommended his dismissal, but an imperial edict specially spared him.

sentences.zh: 既受代，行至歸德，疏陳四事，請崇聖學；

translations.literal: After his successor took over, when he reached Guide he memorialized on four matters, asking that sacred learning be honored;
translations.idiomatic: After his replacement took office, en route to Guide he submitted a memorial on four matters, urging greater respect for classical learning;

sentences.zh: 議政親臣專心國事；

translations.literal: that close ministers in counsel should devote themselves to state affairs;
translations.idiomatic: that the emperor's trusted advisers should give their full attention to affairs of state;

sentences.zh: 用人宜審；

translations.literal: that appointments should be made with care;
translations.idiomatic: that appointments should be made with greater care;

sentences.zh: 聽言宜斷：上嘉納之。

translations.literal: that counsel should be heard and decided upon: the emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: and that the throne should hear counsel and act decisively—the emperor praised and accepted the memorial.

sentences.zh: 復奏苗練終難就撫。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that Miao's militia would ultimately be impossible to pacify.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another memorial arguing that Miao's militia could never truly be brought to heel.

sentences.zh: 二年春，沛霖复叛，圍蒙城，群捻助之，詔甲三在籍會籌防剿。

translations.literal: In the spring of the second year Peilin rebelled again, besieged Mengcheng, and the Nian bands aided him; Jiasan was ordered, while at home, to help plan defense and suppression.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the second year Peilin rebelled again and besieged Mengcheng with Nian bands in support; Jiasan, though at home, was ordered to help plan the defense and suppression.

sentences.zh: 臨淮軍苦飢乏。

translations.literal: The Linhuai army suffered bitter hunger and want.
translations.idiomatic: The army at Linhuai was starving and desperately short of supplies.

sentences.zh: 甲三奉命急籌接濟，乃倡捐募敢死士出間道，運至蒙城。

translations.literal: Jiasan, ordered to rush relief, then raised donations to recruit dare-to-die men who took secret routes to bring supplies to Mengcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Ordered to rush relief, Jiasan raised donations and recruited volunteers willing to die for the cause, who slipped through bypaths to get supplies to Mengcheng.

sentences.zh: 捻匪兩犯陳州，甲三病已亟，榻前授將吏方略，擊走之。

translations.literal: The Nian twice invaded Chenzhou; Jiasan was already desperately ill, yet from his couch he taught generals and officials their strategy, and they drove the invaders off.
translations.idiomatic: The Nian struck Chenzhou twice; though Jiasan was near death, he dictated strategy from his sickbed to his officers, and they drove the rebels off.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，優詔賜卹，諡端敏。

translations.literal: He soon died; a special edict granted mourning honors, and his posthumous title was Duanmin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died. The court issued a special edict granting mourning honors and gave him the posthumous title Duanmin.

sentences.zh: 擢其子保恆侍講學士，保齡內閣中書。

translations.literal: His son Bao Heng was promoted to reader in the Hanlin Academy, and Baoling was made a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao Heng was promoted to reader in the Hanlin Academy, and Baoling was appointed a secretary in the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 陳州、臨淮、淮安並建專祠。

translations.literal: Dedicated shrines were built at Chenzhou, Linhuai, and Huai'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dedicated shrines were erected at Chenzhou, Linhuai, and Huai'an.

sentences.zh: 後淮安請祀名宦，河南請祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: Later Huai'an requested his enshrinement among distinguished officials, and Henan among worthy locals.
translations.idiomatic: Later Huai'an petitioned to enshrine him among distinguished officials, and Henan among local worthies.

sentences.zh: 子保恆，字小午，道光三十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: His son Bao Heng, styled Xiaowu, passed the jinshi in the thirtieth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed compiling editor.
translations.idiomatic: His son Bao Heng, whose style was Xiaowu, became a jinshi in the thirtieth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a compiling editor.

sentences.zh: 從父軍中，咸豐五年，詔允留軍差遣。

translations.literal: Serving in his father's army, in the fifth year of Xianfeng an edict allowed him to remain with the army on assignment.
translations.idiomatic: He served in his father's army, and in the fifth year of Xianfeng an edict permitted him to remain with the army on active duty.

sentences.zh: 七年，從解亳州圍，拔白龍王廟、寺兒集、雉河集賊壘，進攻三圩，戰最力。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he helped lift the siege of Bozhou, took the rebel strongholds at White Dragon King Temple, Sierji, and Zhiheji, pressed the attack on three stockades, and fought with the greatest vigor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he helped lift the Bozhou siege, captured the rebel strongholds at White Dragon King Temple, Sierji, and Zhiheji, pressed the attack on three stockades, and fought harder than anyone.

sentences.zh: 勝保以聞，加侍講銜，賜花翎。

translations.literal: Sheng Bao reported this; he was given the rank of reader and granted the peacock feather.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao reported his deeds; he received the rank of reader and was granted the peacock feather.

sentences.zh: 八年，會攻懷遠捻首李大喜，奪其輜重，又大破孫葵心、劉狗於太和，賜號伊勒圖巴圖魯。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he joined the attack on Nian chief Li Daxi at Huaiyuan and seized his baggage train, then routed Sun Kuixin and Liu Gou at Taihe and was granted the title Yiletu Baturu.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined the attack on Nian leader Li Daxi at Huaiyuan and seized his baggage train, then crushed Sun Kuixin and Liu Gou at Taihe and was granted the title Yiletu Baturu.

sentences.zh: 九年，甲三罷軍事，保恆回京供職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Jiasan left military affairs, and Bao Heng returned to the capital for his regular post.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Jiasan left military command, and Bao Heng returned to the capital to resume his court duties.

sentences.zh: 十年，復命保恆赴甲三軍，破賊定遠，幫辦軍務穆騰阿上其功，甲三力辭，上諭甲三不必引嫌。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Bao Heng was again ordered to Jiasan's army; they broke the rebels at Dingyuan; Muteng'e, assisting military affairs, reported his merit; Jiasan strongly declined on grounds of favoritism, but the emperor told Jiasan not to cite that scruple.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Bao Heng was again sent to Jiasan's army; they defeated the rebels at Dingyuan, and Muteng'e, who was assisting military affairs, reported his merit. Jiasan strongly objected on grounds of nepotism, but the emperor told him not to plead conflict of interest.

sentences.zh: 十一年，破苗沛霖黨張士端於懷遠，會克定遠。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he defeated Peilin's follower Zhang Shiduan at Huaiyuan and jointly took Dingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he defeated Peilin's follower Zhang Shiduan at Huaiyuan and helped take Dingyuan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年，連擢侍講、侍讀、庶子。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tongzhi he was promoted in succession to reader, senior reader, and household steward of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tongzhi he rose in quick succession to reader, senior reader, and household steward of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 甲三以病解職，命保恆仍留軍。

translations.literal: Jiasan resigned on grounds of illness; Bao Heng was ordered to remain with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiasan resigned because of illness, Bao Heng was ordered to stay with the army.

sentences.zh: 尋丁繼母憂，歸。

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his stepmother and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon went into mourning for his stepmother and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二年，從甲三督治陳州團防。

translations.literal: In the second year he followed Jiasan in supervising Chenzhou militia defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he joined Jiasan in overseeing Chenzhou's militia defenses.

sentences.zh: 甲三尋卒，卹典推恩，命保恆以侍講學士即補。

translations.literal: Jiasan soon died; mourning honors were extended, and Bao Heng was ordered to fill immediately the post of reader in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan soon died; the court extended mourning honors and ordered Bao Heng to step directly into the post of Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 淮北初平，保恆疏陳善後八策，請以逆產、絕產募民屯墾，整頓兩淮鹽務，以濟屯田經費；

translations.literal: With northern Huai newly pacified, Bao Heng memorialized eight recovery policies, asking to recruit settlers with confiscated and ownerless land for colonization and to overhaul the Two Huai salt administration to fund colonization;
translations.idiomatic: With northern Huai newly pacified, Bao Heng submitted eight recovery policies, proposing to recruit settlers with confiscated and ownerless land and to reform the Two Huai salt trade to finance the colonization effort;

sentences.zh: 又密陳李世忠驕恣難制，請加裁抑。

translations.literal: He also secretly memorialized that Li Shizhong was proud and uncontrollable and asked that he be restrained.
translations.idiomatic: He also secretly reported that Li Shizhong had grown arrogant and ungovernable and asked that he be brought under tighter control.

sentences.zh: 三年，保恆以屯田議未即行，請詣京與廷臣面議。

translations.literal: In the third year, because the colonization plan had not been promptly carried out, Bao Heng asked to go to the capital to discuss it face to face with court ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, because the colonization plan had not been put into effect, Bao Heng asked to go to the capital and discuss it in person with the ministers.

sentences.zh: 詔斥不諳體制，下部議降一級，以鴻臚寺少卿候補。

translations.literal: An edict rebuked him for not understanding protocol; the Board recommended demoting him one grade to await appointment as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: An edict rebuked him for failing to understand proper procedure; the Board recommended demoting him one grade to await appointment as vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 服闋赴京，廷臣交薦其才。

translations.literal: After his mourning period he went to the capital, and court ministers successively recommended his talent.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning ended he went to the capital, and ministers one after another praised his ability.

sentences.zh: 七年，捻匪犯畿輔，保恆自請效力戎行，命赴李鴻章軍委用。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, when the Nian invaded the capital region, Bao Heng volunteered for military service and was ordered to Li Hongzhang's army for assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when the Nian raided the capital region, Bao Heng volunteered for active service and was assigned to Li Hongzhang's army.

sentences.zh: 捻平，加三品銜，授侍講學士。

translations.literal: When the Nian were pacified he received third-grade rank and was appointed reader in the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: After the Nian were suppressed he received third-grade rank and was appointed Hanlin reader.

sentences.zh: 從陝甘總督左宗棠赴陝西，八年，命筦西征糧台，許專摺奏事。

translations.literal: He followed Shaanxi-Gansu governor Zuo Zongtang to Shaanxi; in the eighth year he was ordered to manage the western expedition grain bureau and was permitted to submit memorials on his own authority.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Shaanxi-Gansu governor Zuo Zongtang to Shaanxi, and in the eighth year was put in charge of the western expedition grain bureau with permission to submit memorials directly to the throne.

sentences.zh: 十一年，遷詹事。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to junior tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to junior tutor.

sentences.zh: 肅州克復，加頭品頂戴。

translations.literal: When Suzhou was recovered he received the first-rank official's hat ornament.
translations.idiomatic: When Suzhou was recovered he was granted the first-rank official's hat ornament.

sentences.zh: 十三年，連擢內閣學士、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he rose in succession to grand secretary and vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he rose in quick succession to grand secretary and vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 保恆督餉凡五載，諸軍欠餉糾轕，騰挪無缺。

translations.literal: Bao Heng supervised supplies for five years; though the armies' unpaid rations were tangled in dispute, he juggled funds without shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Heng oversaw supplies for five years; though pay and rations owed to the armies were a snarl of claims, he shifted funds so that nothing ran dry.

sentences.zh: 及大軍出關，詔襄辦左宗棠轉餉事，進駐肅州。

translations.literal: When the main army marched beyond the frontier, he was ordered to assist Zuo Zongtang in forwarding supplies and advanced to garrison at Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the main force marched beyond the frontier, he was ordered to help Zuo Zongtang forward supplies and moved forward to garrison Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 保恆請入覲，未許。

translations.literal: Bao Heng asked to attend court in person; permission was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Heng asked to return to court for an audience, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 光緒元年，召回京，兼署吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Guangxu he was recalled to the capital and concurrently served as acting vice minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Guangxu he was recalled to the capital and concurrently served as acting vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 二年，調刑部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to vice minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to vice minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 保恆久歷兵間，審於世變，屢上疏論時事，請辨人材，厲士氣，收人心，言甚切直。

translations.literal: Long seasoned in war and alert to changing times, Bao Heng repeatedly memorialized on current affairs, urging discernment of talent, strengthening morale, and winning hearts; his words were very forthright.
translations.idiomatic: Long tested in war and keenly aware of how the world was changing, Bao Heng repeatedly memorialized on current affairs, urging the court to judge men rightly, stiffen public morale, and win people's loyalty; his language was blunt and forceful.

sentences.zh: 又言：「歷觀各國情形，惟俄為最強最狡，往往不動聲色，佈局於十數年以前，肆毒於十數年以後。

translations.literal: He also said: "Surveying the conditions of every country, Russia alone is strongest and craftiest, often laying plans in silence a dozen years ahead and unleashing harm a dozen years later.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Looking across the nations, Russia alone is the strongest and the most cunning. Again and again it lays its plans in silence a decade or more in advance, then strikes a decade or more later.

sentences.zh: 履霜有像，桑土宜先。

translations.literal: Frost underfoot has its signs; mulberry bark should be gathered first.
translations.idiomatic: "When frost is coming, the signs appear early; the wise gather mulberry bark before the storm.

sentences.zh: 伏原特簡久經戰陣熟習韜略之治兵重臣，專辦東三省練兵事務。

translations.literal: I humbly ask that a senior official long experienced in war and well versed in strategy be specially chosen to manage military training in the Three Eastern Provinces.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly ask that a senior official of proven battlefield experience and deep knowledge of strategy be specially chosen to oversee military training in the Three Eastern Provinces.

sentences.zh: 凡屬兵馬餉糈邊防之事，悉以屬之。

translations.literal: All matters of troops, horses, pay, grain, and frontier defense should be entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: Every matter touching troops, horses, pay, grain, and frontier defense should be placed under his authority.

sentences.zh: 重以事權，寬以歲月，無事則可消覬覦之萌，有事則可為撻伐之助。

translations.literal: Given heavy authority and ample time, in peace he could still the first stirrings of covetous eyes; in war he could aid in punitive campaigns.
translations.idiomatic: Give him real power and enough time: in peace he can cut off greed before it takes root; in war he can strengthen our hand for punitive action.

sentences.zh: 用以拱衛神京，懾服他族。

translations.literal: Thus to shield the sacred capital and overawe other peoples.
translations.idiomatic: In this way the sacred capital would be shielded and other peoples held in awe.

sentences.zh: 根本至計，未可委之一二不相統轄之武臣，謂可威強鄰而彌外患也。

translations.literal: This is a root policy; it cannot be entrusted to one or two military men who do not answer to a single chain of command, yet be expected to awe strong neighbors and quell external trouble.
translations.idiomatic: This is a fundamental policy. It cannot be handed to one or two generals who answer to no unified command and still be expected to overawe strong neighbors and settle foreign threats.

sentences.zh: 福建之台灣，僻處海澨，物產豐饒，民、番逼處。

translations.literal: Taiwan in Fujian lies remote on the coast, rich in products, with Han settlers and aborigines living cheek by jowl.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan, part of Fujian, sits far out on the coast. Its products are abundant, and Han settlers and indigenous peoples live pressed close together.

sentences.zh: 非專駐大臣，鎮以重兵，孚以威信，舉民風、吏治、營製、鄉團，事事實力整頓，未易為功。

translations.literal: Without a resident commissioner, garrisoned heavy forces, and established authority, and real effort in reforming popular custom, official governance, camp discipline, and local militia, success will not come easily.
translations.idiomatic: Without a resident commissioner backed by a strong garrison and real authority, and without hard work on popular custom, official governance, military discipline, and local militia, little can be achieved.

sentences.zh: 若以福建巡撫每歲半載駐台，恐閩中全省之政務，道路懸隔，而轉就拋荒。

translations.literal: If the Fujian governor spends only half the year in Taiwan, I fear the whole province's administration, cut off by distance, will in turn be neglected.
translations.idiomatic: If the Fujian governor spends only half the year in Taiwan, I fear that the rest of the province, cut off by distance, will in turn be neglected.

sentences.zh: 台灣甫定之規模，去住無常，而終為具文。

translations.literal: Taiwan's newly settled order, with comings and goings unsettled, would in the end remain empty form.
translations.idiomatic: Taiwan's newly established order, with its governor coming and going at whim, would in the end exist only on paper.

sentences.zh: 請改福建巡撫為台灣巡撫，駐台灣，而以總督辦福建全省事，各專責成。

translations.literal: I ask that the Fujian governor be changed to governor of Taiwan, resident in Taiwan, while the governor-general handles all Fujian affairs, each with clear responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the post of Fujian governor be changed to governor of Taiwan, resident in Taiwan, while the governor-general handles all affairs of Fujian proper—each with a clear mandate.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，下部議行。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it was referred to the Board for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, it was referred to the Board for deliberation and implementation.

sentences.zh: 三年，河南大旱，命保恆襄辦賑務。

translations.literal: In the third year Henan suffered great drought; Bao Heng was ordered to assist in relief work.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year a great drought struck Henan, and Bao Heng was ordered to assist with famine relief.

sentences.zh: 既至，疏陳沿途流民狀，先令州縣停徵。

translations.literal: On arrival he memorialized on the condition of refugees along the route and first ordered prefectures and counties to suspend tax collection.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival he reported on the refugees he had seen along the way and first ordered prefectures and counties to suspend tax collection.

sentences.zh: 四年，奏請截留江南漕糧九萬石，不許；

translations.literal: In the fourth year he memorialized to retain ninety thousand shi of Jiangnan grain tribute; this was not permitted;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he asked to retain ninety thousand shi of Jiangnan grain tribute; the request was denied;

sentences.zh: 請借直隸平糶餘米三萬石，許之。

translations.literal: He asked to borrow thirty thousand shi of surplus grain from Zhili's relief sales; this was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: he asked to borrow thirty thousand shi of surplus grain from Zhili's relief granaries; that was granted.

sentences.zh: 又請借用江蘇義倉積穀及台灣捐修鐵路洋銀五十萬圓，下部議。

translations.literal: He also asked to borrow Jiangsu charity-granary reserves and five hundred thousand dollars in foreign silver from Taiwan's railway repair fund; this was referred to the Board.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked to borrow grain from Jiangsu's charity granaries and five hundred thousand foreign silver dollars from Taiwan's railway repair fund; the matter was referred to the Board.

sentences.zh: 令籌歸還之法。

translations.literal: He was ordered to devise a method of repayment.
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to work out a plan for repayment.

sentences.zh: 保恆請緩禁川鹽行楚，加抽鹽釐，備抵賑需，為兩全之計。

translations.literal: Bao Heng asked to relax the ban on Sichuan salt entering Hubei, add salt levies, and use the proceeds for relief—a plan to serve both ends.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Heng proposed easing the ban on Sichuan salt in Hubei, adding a salt surcharge, and using the revenue for famine relief—a compromise meant to serve both needs.

sentences.zh: 疏入，仍下部議。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, it was again referred to the Board.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, it was again referred to the Board for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 保恆查賑所至，屏絕供張，服食粗糲，刊賑章二十二則頒行，就孔道設粥廠，就食省城者凡十餘萬人，棲息得所。

translations.literal: Wherever Bao Heng inspected relief he rejected official entertainment, ate coarse food, published twenty-two relief regulations, set soup kitchens along major roads, and more than a hundred thousand people who came to the provincial capital for food found shelter.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Bao Heng went on relief duty he refused official receptions, lived on plain food, issued twenty-two relief regulations, set up soup kitchens along the main roads, and gave more than a hundred thousand refugees who came to the provincial capital for food a place to stay.

sentences.zh: 時親視察，感疫病卒，優詔賜卹，諡文誠。

translations.literal: While personally inspecting he contracted epidemic disease and died; a special edict granted mourning honors, and his posthumous title was Wencheng.
translations.idiomatic: While making the rounds in person he caught an epidemic disease and died. The court issued a special edict granting mourning honors and gave him the posthumous title Wencheng.

sentences.zh: 河南省城建專祠，附祀陳州、臨淮甲三祠。

translations.literal: A dedicated shrine was built in Henan province, affiliated with the Jiasan shrines at Chenzhou and Linhuai.
translations.idiomatic: A dedicated shrine was built in Henan province, attached to the Jiasan shrines at Chenzhou and Linhuai.

sentences.zh: 毛昶熙，字旭初，河南武陟人。

translations.literal: Mao Changxi, styled Xuchu, was a native of Wuzhi in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Mao Changxi, whose style was Xuchu, came from Wuzhi in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父樹棠，官至戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: His father Shutang rose to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shutang rose to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 昶熙，道光二十五年進士，選庶吉士，授檢討，咸豐五年，遷御史，轉給事中。

translations.literal: Changxi passed the jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, was appointed reviser; in the fifth year of Xianfeng he was transferred to censor and then supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi became a jinshi in the twenty-fifth year of Daoguang, entered the Hanlin as a bachelor, and was appointed a reviser; in the fifth year of Xianfeng he was moved to censor and then supervising secretary.

sentences.zh: 屢上疏論軍事吏治，劾步軍統領聯順徇私廢治，罷之，甚負清望。

translations.literal: He repeatedly memorialized on military affairs and official governance, impeached metropolitan garrison commander Lianshun for favoritism that ruined administration and had him dismissed, and earned great repute for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized on military affairs and official discipline, impeached metropolitan garrison commander Lianshun for favoritism that had ruined governance, and got him dismissed—winning wide respect for his integrity.

sentences.zh: 八年，授順天府丞，胡林翼密疏薦之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed vice magistrate of Shuntian prefecture; Hu Linyi privately recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed vice magistrate of Shuntian prefecture on Hu Linyi's confidential recommendation.

sentences.zh: 十年，加左副都御史銜，命督辦河南團練，至則規畫全局，定條規十二事：築堡寨，扼要隘，擇首事，選團丁，籌公費，互救援，定約束，申號令，公賞罰，詰姦宄，旌忠義，而終之以實力奉行；

translations.literal: In the tenth year he received the nominal rank of left vice censor-in-chief and was ordered to supervise Henan militia training; on arrival he mapped the whole situation and fixed twelve regulations: build forts and stockades, hold strategic passes, choose leaders, select militiamen, raise public funds, mutual rescue, fixed rules, clear orders, open rewards and punishments, investigate traitors, honor loyalty and righteousness—and ended with earnest enforcement;
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he received the nominal rank of left vice censor-in-chief and was ordered to supervise Henan militia training. On arrival he mapped the whole situation and laid down twelve rules: build forts and stockades, hold strategic passes, choose leaders, select militiamen, raise public funds, aid one another in emergencies, set clear constraints, enforce commands, make rewards and punishments public, root out traitors, honor loyalty and righteousness—and above all, carry them out in earnest;

sentences.zh: 並疏陳調練民勇苦累之弊，亟宜改辦鄉團，以紓民力。

translations.literal: He also memorialized on the hardship of mobilizing trained militia and urgently asked to shift to local militia corps to ease the people's burden.
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized on the crushing burden of mobilizing trained militia and urged an immediate shift to local militia corps to relieve the people.

sentences.zh: 尋命督辦剿匪事宜，駐軍歸德。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to supervise bandit suppression and garrisoned at Guide.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to supervise bandit suppression and established his headquarters at Guide.

sentences.zh: 亳州捻匪犯鹿邑，督練勇擊走之，分路馳剿，九戰皆捷。

translations.literal: Bozhou Nian invaded Luyi; he led militia to drive them off and pursued on separate routes; nine battles all victorious.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozhou Nian raided Luyi, he led militia to beat them back and pursued them on separate routes, winning nine battles in a row.

sentences.zh: 十一年，疏言：「捻騎逾萬，官軍馬隊過單，皖、豫交界之區，皆平原曠野，步隊無以製賊死命。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "Nian horsemen exceed ten thousand; government cavalry is too few; the border region of Anhui and Henan is all flat open country—infantry cannot strike the rebels a mortal blow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he memorialized: "The Nian field more than ten thousand horsemen, while our cavalry is far too thin. The Anhui-Henan borderlands are open plain—foot soldiers cannot destroy the enemy outright.

sentences.zh: 今豫境修築寨堡，已有成效，應責令寨長各選壯丁一名、馬一匹，投效來營。

translations.literal: Now fort and stockade building in Henan has already shown results; stockade chiefs should each be charged to select one sturdy man and one horse to report for duty at camp.
translations.idiomatic: Fort and stockade building in Henan is already proving effective. Each stockade chief should be ordered to select one able-bodied man and one horse to report for service in camp.

sentences.zh: 歸、陳兩屬，約可得馬隊三四百名。

translations.literal: From the two jurisdictions of Guide and Chen, one could obtain roughly three to four hundred cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In Guide and Chen prefectures alone, roughly three to four hundred mounted men could be raised.

sentences.zh: 」上命推廣其法行之。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered that his method be promoted and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered that this plan be extended and put into practice.

sentences.zh: 捻匪偪省城，圍通許，昶熙檄軍援之，圍立解。

translations.literal: Nian bandits pressed the provincial capital and besieged Tongxu; Changxi dispatched troops to rescue it, and the siege was immediately lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When Nian rebels threatened the provincial capital and encircled Tongxu, Changxi sent troops to relieve the town, and the siege was quickly broken.

sentences.zh: 因疏言：「軍令不一，將士無所適從，宜會合撫臣以一事權。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized: "Military orders are not unified; officers and soldiers have nothing to follow. The governor should be brought in to consolidate command authority.
translations.idiomatic: He therefore memorialized: "With military orders divided, officers and soldiers do not know whom to obey. Command should be consolidated under the provincial governor."

sentences.zh: 」上命巡撫嚴樹森督辦河南剿匪事宜，昶熙副之，仍兼辦團練。

translations.literal: " The Emperor ordered Governor Yan Shusen to supervise Henan bandit suppression, with Changxi as his deputy while continuing to oversee militia training.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Governor Yan Shusen to take charge of suppressing bandits in Henan, with Changxi as his deputy while he continued to oversee militia training.

sentences.zh: 三月，克唐縣。

translations.literal: In the third month, Tang County was captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, government forces took Tang County.

sentences.zh: 捻匪趙國良犯光州，陳大喜犯汝陽，並擊走之。

translations.literal: The Nian rebel Zhao Guoliang attacked Guangzhou, and Chen Daxi attacked Ruyang; he drove off both.
translations.idiomatic: When the Nian chiefs Zhao Guoliang and Chen Daxi raided Guangzhou and Ruyang, he defeated and drove off both forces.

sentences.zh: 尋以誤用逃犯李占標，降三級調用，暫免開缺。

translations.literal: Soon afterward, for mistakenly employing the escaped convict Li Zhanbiao, he was demoted three ranks and transferred, but temporarily spared from vacating his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon demoted three ranks and transferred for having mistakenly employed the fugitive Li Zhanbiao, though he was temporarily allowed to remain in office.

sentences.zh: 大河以南府、廳、州、縣團練皆成立，屢敗賊，詔開復處分。

translations.literal: South of the Yellow River, militia in every prefecture, sub-prefecture, department, and county had been established; they repeatedly defeated the bandits, and an edict restored him from punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Militia had been established in every prefecture, sub-prefecture, department, and county south of the Yellow River, and after they repeatedly defeated the rebels, an edict restored him to his former rank.

sentences.zh: 連擢順天府尹、太僕寺卿、內閣學士，仍留軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to Shuntian prefect, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and Grand Secretary, while remaining with the army.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in quick succession to Shuntian prefect, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Stud, and Grand Secretary, yet was kept in the field.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，昶熙請謁文宗梓宮，面陳機要，未許，命以軍事密疏入告。
