translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Changxi requested to visit Emperor Wenzong's coffin and present crucial matters in person; this was not granted, and he was ordered to report on military affairs through confidential memorials.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Muzong took the throne, Changxi asked to visit Emperor Wenzong's coffin and present urgent matters in person. The request was denied, and he was told to report military affairs through confidential memorials instead.

sentences.zh: 疏上製捻要策，略曰：「年來剿捻未得要領，其誤有二：一在專言防堵。

translations.literal: In a memorial on the essential strategy for suppressing the Nian, he wrote in summary: "In recent years the campaign against the Nian has missed the point. The errors are two. The first is to speak only of blocking and containment.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial outlining the essential strategy for suppressing the Nian, stating in summary: "For years the campaign against the Nian has missed the point. There are two mistakes. The first is to rely solely on blocking and containment.

sentences.zh: 潁、徐、歸、陳，平原千里，無險可扼，捻數路同發，分而愈多。

translations.literal: Ying, Xu, Gui, and Chen are flat plains for a thousand li, with no terrain to hold. The Nian launch on many routes at once, and the more they are divided, the more numerous they become.
translations.idiomatic: Ying, Xu, Gui, and Chen form a thousand li of open plain with no defensible ground. The Nian strike on many routes at once, and the more they are split up, the more numerous they become.

sentences.zh: 官軍分堵則兵單，合堵則力疏，猶之院無牆垣，徒守門戶，不能遏盜也。

translations.literal: If government troops are split to block them, their forces are too thin; if combined to block them, their strength is spread too wide. It is like a courtyard with no walls, guarding only the gate—thieves cannot be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: If government troops are split to block the Nian, their forces are too thin; if massed to block them, their strength is spread too thin. It is like a courtyard with no walls, guarding only the gate—no way to stop thieves from getting in.

sentences.zh: 一在無成算而輕戰。

translations.literal: The second is to fight rashly without a settled plan.
translations.idiomatic: The second is to engage in battle rashly, without a settled plan.

sentences.zh: 賊眾數倍於我，馬則十倍過之。

translations.literal: The rebels outnumber us several times over, and in horses they exceed us tenfold.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels outnumber us several times over, and their cavalry exceeds ours tenfold.

sentences.zh: 我無必勝之術，僥倖一戰，一旦敗潰，賊焰愈張。

translations.literal: We have no sure method of victory. If we gamble on one battle and are once routed, the rebels' momentum will grow all the stronger.
translations.idiomatic: We have no sure way to win. If we gamble on a single battle and are routed, the rebels' momentum will only grow.

sentences.zh: 至會師搗老巢，實為平賊要策。

translations.literal: As for assembling armies to strike their old nests, that is in truth the essential strategy for pacifying the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: As for massing armies to strike the rebels' strongholds, that is indeed the essential strategy for pacifying them.

sentences.zh: 皖捻雖以張洛行為主，而陳、宋、潁、壽、淮、徐方數百里，無處非賊巢，即無處無賊首。

translations.literal: Although the Anhui Nian chiefly follow Zhang Luoxing, across Chen, Song, Ying, Shou, Huai, and Xu, for several hundred li there is no place that is not a bandit nest, and no place without a bandit chief.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Anhui Nian are led chiefly by Zhang Luoxing, across Chen, Song, Ying, Shou, Huai, and Xu—hundreds of li of territory—there is scarcely a place that is not a rebel nest or without a rebel leader.

sentences.zh: 官軍即能次第掃除，勢難刻期淨盡。

translations.literal: Even if government troops can clear them one by one, it will be hard to finish the task entirely on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Even if government troops can mop them up one by one, it will be nearly impossible to eliminate them all within a set time.

sentences.zh: 若繞過小捻，徑搗大捻老巢，捨近攻遠，而近賊襲我於後，我必不支，此會搗老巢之難遽奏效也。

translations.literal: If we bypass the smaller Nian bands and strike directly at the larger nests, abandoning what is near to attack what is far, while nearby bandits strike us from behind, we surely cannot hold. This is why a joint assault on the old nests is hard to bring to quick effect.
translations.idiomatic: If we bypass smaller Nian bands to strike the main strongholds directly—abandoning what is near to attack what is far—nearby rebels will hit us from behind and we will not be able to hold. That is why a mass assault on the rebels' nests is hard to bring off quickly.

sentences.zh: 然捻匪與粵匪不同，粵匪蜂屯蟻聚，其勢合；

translations.literal: Yet the Nian differ from the Cantonese rebels: the Cantonese swarm together like bees and ants, and their force is united;
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Nian differ from the Cantonese rebels. The Cantonese mass together like bees and ants, and their force is united;

sentences.zh: 捻匪散處各圩，其勢分。

translations.literal: the Nian are scattered among various stockades, and their force is divided.
translations.idiomatic: the Nian are scattered among separate stockades, and their force is divided.

sentences.zh: 其出竄也，必須裝旗糾合各圩賊目，約期會舉，常十餘日始得出。

translations.literal: When they sally forth, they must raise banners to gather the chiefs of the various stockades and agree on a date to act together; it often takes more than ten days before they can set out.
translations.idiomatic: When they raid abroad, they must raise banners to summon the chiefs of the various stockades and agree on a date to move together; it often takes more than ten days before they can set out.

sentences.zh: 其竄山東者，每會於保安山、龍山；

translations.literal: Those raiding Shandong meet each time at Bao'an Mountain and Long Mountain;
translations.idiomatic: Those raiding into Shandong gather at Bao'an Mountain and Long Mountain;

sentences.zh: 竄汴梁者，會於小奈集、大寺集；

translations.literal: those raiding Bianliang meet at Xiao Naiji and Da Siji;
translations.idiomatic: those raiding toward Bianliang gather at Xiao Naiji and Da Siji;

sentences.zh: 竄陳州者，會於南十字河、張信溜：地皆偪近亳州，亳州者，賊之吭也。

translations.literal: those raiding Chenzhou meet at Nan Shizihe and Zhang Xinliu: all these places lie close to Bozhou, and Bozhou is the rebels' throat.
translations.idiomatic: those raiding toward Chenzhou gather at Nan Shizihe and Zhang Xinliu. All these places lie close to Bozhou—and Bozhou is the rebels' jugular.

sentences.zh: 計莫若擇重臣素有威望者，統步隊數万、馬隊數千，屯軍於此。

translations.literal: The best plan is to choose a senior minister of long-standing prestige, command tens of thousands of infantry and thousands of cavalry, and garrison the army here.
translations.idiomatic: The best plan is to appoint a senior minister of established prestige, give him command of tens of thousands of infantry and thousands of cavalry, and station the army here.

sentences.zh: 用伍員多方誤楚之法，分所部為數起，此歸彼出，此出彼歸，循環馳突於各捻賊圩之間，使大捻無從勾結，小捻聲息不通，惴惴焉日防官兵之至，自不能裝旗出竄，四出打糧。

translations.literal: Using Wu Yuan's method of misleading Chu on many fronts, divide the forces into several columns—when one returns the other sallies, wheeling in repeated raids among the Nian stockades—so that the larger bands cannot link up, the smaller bands cannot pass word, and in daily dread of the arrival of government troops they cannot raise banners to raid or forage in all directions.
translations.idiomatic: Using Wu Yuan's tactic of misleading the enemy on many fronts, divide the force into several columns that rotate in and out—when one rests the other strikes—wheeling in repeated raids among the Nian stockades. The larger bands will be unable to link up, the smaller bands unable to communicate, and trembling daily at the approach of government troops, they will be unable to raise banners, raid abroad, or forage in all directions.

sentences.zh: 俟其飢困，然後以重兵次第圍剿。

translations.literal: Wait until they are hungry and exhausted, then with heavy troops encircle and suppress them in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: Wait until hunger and exhaustion set in, then use heavy forces to encircle and suppress them one by one.

sentences.zh: 賊無外援，則小股膽落，大股易平，招撫兼施，立可解散，不必盡煩兵力矣。

translations.literal: With no outside support, the smaller bands will lose heart, the larger bands will be easy to pacify, and with persuasion and suppression combined they can quickly be dissolved—there is no need to exhaust all military force.
translations.idiomatic: Cut off from outside support, smaller bands will lose heart and larger bands will be easier to crush. With persuasion and force combined, they can quickly be broken up, without having to commit the full army.

sentences.zh: 夫防賊於既出之後，何如遏賊於未出之先？

translations.literal: To defend against bandits after they have already sallied forth—how does that compare with stopping them before they sally forth?
translations.idiomatic: What is the point of defending against rebels after they have already sallied forth, when it is better to stop them before they can?

sentences.zh: 勦賊於既聚之餘，何如蹙賊以難聚之勢？

translations.literal: To suppress bandits after they have already gathered—how does that compare with pressing them into a situation where gathering is difficult?
translations.idiomatic: What is the point of suppressing rebels after they have already massed, when it is better to keep them from gathering in the first place?

sentences.zh: 而又無勞師襲遠之危、輕進損威之失，所謂不戰而屈人之兵者是也。

translations.literal: Moreover, without the danger of a distant expedition or the loss of prestige from rash advance—this is what is meant by subduing the enemy without fighting.
translations.idiomatic: And all this without the risk of a distant expedition or the loss of prestige from rash advances—this is what is meant by defeating the enemy without fighting.

sentences.zh: 今日大計，以衛畿輔固根本為先。

translations.literal: Today's great plan must put first the defense of the capital region and the securing of the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Today's paramount strategy is to defend the capital region and secure the foundations of the realm.

sentences.zh: 豫東者，畿輔之門戶也。

translations.literal: Eastern Henan is the gateway to the capital region.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Henan is the gateway to the capital region.

sentences.zh: 亳州者，豫東之賊源也。

translations.literal: Bozhou is the source of bandits in eastern Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou is the fountainhead of rebellion in eastern Henan.

sentences.zh: 亳州之賊不除，則豫東之匪難絕，即畿輔之地不安。

translations.literal: If the bandits of Bozhou are not eliminated, banditry in eastern Henan cannot be ended, and even the capital region will not be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If the rebels at Bozhou are not eliminated, banditry in eastern Henan cannot be stamped out, and the capital region itself will remain insecure.

sentences.zh: 重兵駐豫，不能兼顧東省，駐東亦不能兼顧豫防。

translations.literal: If heavy troops are stationed in Henan, they cannot also guard Shandong; if stationed in Shandong, they cannot also guard Henan's defenses.
translations.idiomatic: Heavy forces stationed in Henan cannot also cover Shandong, and forces stationed in Shandong cannot also cover Henan.

sentences.zh: 惟亳為諸捻匯處之區，拔本塞源，實在於此。

translations.literal: Only Bozhou is the place where all the Nian converge; to uproot the source and stop the flow, the key truly lies here.
translations.idiomatic: Bozhou alone is where all the Nian converge. To uproot the problem at its source, the key lies here.

sentences.zh: 且蒙、亳百姓，祗以偪處賊巢，呼訴無門，不得不苟全性命，非盡甘心為逆也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the people of Meng and Bozhou, living pressed against bandit nests with nowhere to appeal, have had no choice but to preserve their lives as best they can—they are not all willingly rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the people of Meng and Bozhou live pressed against rebel strongholds with nowhere to turn for justice. They have had no choice but to save their lives as best they can—not all of them willingly joined the rebels.

sentences.zh: 若官軍聲勢一振，隨撫隨剿，不但忠義良民同心殺賊，即附賊之堡寨，亦相率就撫，輔助官兵。

translations.literal: If the prestige of the government army rises once, pacifying while suppressing, not only will loyal people unite in killing bandits, but even stockades attached to the bandits will submit in numbers and assist the government troops.
translations.idiomatic: If government forces once regain their momentum, combining pacification with suppression, not only will loyal commoners unite to kill rebels, but even stockades that had sided with the bandits will submit in numbers and aid the army.

sentences.zh: 彼久經兵革之地，人習戰爭，附賊則為悍賊，反正則為勁兵，奪賊焰而益軍威，計無便於此者。

translations.literal: In lands long ravaged by war, the people are practiced in fighting. Attached to bandits they become fierce bandits; turned right they become strong soldiers. To seize the bandits' momentum and increase military prestige, there is no plan more convenient than this.
translations.idiomatic: In lands long torn by war, the people know how to fight. Those who side with rebels become fierce fighters; those who come over become strong soldiers. To break the rebels' momentum and strengthen the army, there is no better plan.

sentences.zh: 前勝保、袁甲三累獲大勝，皆由屯駐亳州，扼其要害，並賴關保、德楞額馬隊之力，是以所向有功。

translations.literal: Previously Sheng Bao and Yuan Jiasan repeatedly won great victories, all because they garrisoned at Bozhou and held its key points, and also relied on the cavalry of Guan Bao and Deleng'e—for this reason they succeeded wherever they went.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Bao and Yuan Jiasan won victory after victory precisely because they garrisoned at Bozhou, held its key points, and had the cavalry of Guan Bao and Deleng'e to rely on. That is why they succeeded wherever they fought.

sentences.zh: 前事不遠，可為券證。

translations.literal: Recent events are not far off and can serve as proof.
translations.idiomatic: These recent precedents are close at hand and can serve as proof.

sentences.zh: 」奏入，上韙之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor approved it.

sentences.zh: 時粵、捻合擾潁州，命昶熙出境會剿。

translations.literal: At the time the Cantonese and Nian jointly harassed Yingzhou, and Changxi was ordered to cross the border for a joint campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the Taiping and Nian rebels were jointly raiding Yingzhou, and Changxi was ordered to cross the border to join the campaign.

sentences.zh: 昶熙兵僅五千，且無馬隊，疏請調總兵李續燾等募精壯六千來豫，以厚兵力，如所請行。

translations.literal: Changxi had only five thousand troops and no cavalry. He memorialized requesting that Brigadier Li Xudong and others recruit six thousand elite men to come to Henan to strengthen his forces, and this was granted as requested.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi had only five thousand men and no cavalry. He memorialized asking that Brigadier Li Xudong and others raise six thousand picked troops for Henan to strengthen his force, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 上复敕西安將軍托明阿選西安馬隊一千赴豫。

translations.literal: The Emperor also ordered the Xi'an General Tooming'a to select one thousand Xi'an cavalry and send them to Henan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor also ordered the Xi'an General Tooming'a to select one thousand Xi'an cavalry and dispatch them to Henan.

sentences.zh: 同治元年春，亳捻劉大淵糾黨趨河南，昶熙在省聞警，馳至杞縣，賊已圍城，會僧格林沁軍自山東進至，敗賊許岡，昶熙會所部合擊之，克復所佔民圩，斬馘逾萬，餘賊引去。

translations.literal: In the spring of the first year of the Tongzhi reign, the Bozhou Nian leader Liu Dayuan gathered his followers and marched toward Henan. Changxi, in the provincial capital when the alarm came, rushed to Qixian, where the bandits were already besieging the city. Sengge Rinchen's army arrived from Shandong, defeated the bandits at Xugang, and Changxi joined his own forces in a combined attack. They recovered the civilian stockades the bandits had occupied, killed and beheaded more than ten thousand, and the remaining bandits withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the first year of Tongzhi, the Bozhou Nian chief Liu Dayuan gathered his followers and marched into Henan. Changxi, hearing the alarm while in the provincial capital, rushed to Qixian, where the rebels were already besieging the city. Sengge Rinchen's army arrived from Shandong and defeated the rebels at Xugang; Changxi then joined his own troops in a combined assault. They recovered the civilian stockades the rebels had seized, killed more than ten thousand, and the rest withdrew.

sentences.zh: 檄諸路團勇截殺之，還駐歸德，扼賊歸路。

translations.literal: He dispatched militia on all routes to intercept and kill them, then returned to garrison at Guide and block the bandits' line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered militia on all routes to intercept and cut them down, then returned to garrison at Guide and blocked the rebels' retreat.

sentences.zh: 四月，會同僧軍合擊金樓教匪楊玉驄，盡殲其眾，授禮部侍郎，仍命督團勦賊，歸僧格林沁節制。

translations.literal: In the fourth month, together with Sengge Rinchen's army he jointly attacked the Jinlou sect rebel Yang Yucong and annihilated his entire force. He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, still ordered to supervise militia in suppressing bandits, and placed under Sengge Rinchen's command.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month he joined Sengge Rinchen's army in a combined attack on the Jinlou sect rebel Yang Yucong and wiped out his entire force. He was appointed Vice Minister of Rites, continued to supervise militia operations against the rebels, and was placed under Sengge Rinchen's command.

sentences.zh: 赴汝寧督兵團剿陳大喜諸匪，克正陽，收寨、圩多處。

translations.literal: He went to Runing to supervise troops and militia in suppressing Chen Daxi and other bandits, captured Zhengyang, and recovered many stockades and fortified hamlets.
translations.idiomatic: He went to Runing to direct troops and militia against Chen Daxi and other rebels, took Zhengyang, and recovered numerous stockades and fortified hamlets.

sentences.zh: 二年，誅賊首張鳳林、張福林，克邢集、尚店賊巢，陳大喜竄湖北，汝寧、陳州所屬踞賊，殲除殆盡。

translations.literal: In the second year he executed the bandit chiefs Zhang Fenglin and Zhang Fulin, captured the bandit nests at Xingji and Shangdian, Chen Daxi fled to Hubei, and the bandits holding territory under Runing and Chenzhou were almost entirely wiped out.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he executed the rebel chiefs Zhang Fenglin and Zhang Fulin, took the strongholds at Xingji and Shangdian, and drove Chen Daxi into Hubei. The rebels holding territory under Runing and Chenzhou were nearly all eliminated.

sentences.zh: 調吏部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 亳捻犯陳州，為官軍所扼擊，四竄。

translations.literal: Bozhou Nian invaded Chenzhou, were blocked and struck by government troops, and fled in four directions.
translations.idiomatic: When Bozhou Nian raided Chenzhou, government troops blocked and struck them, and they scattered in all directions.

sentences.zh: 昶熙屯鹿邑，盡平亳北賊寨。

translations.literal: Changxi garrisoned at Luyi and entirely pacified the bandit stockades north of Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi garrisoned at Luyi and completely cleared the rebel stockades north of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，苗沛霖伏誅，淮北肅清。

translations.literal: That winter Miao Peilin was executed in secret, and northern Huai was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Miao Peilin was secretly put to death, and the north Huai region was pacified.

sentences.zh: 詔：「昶熙部勇原助兵力所不足，今兵力足敷應用，飭散遣歸農。

translations.literal: An edict stated: "Changxi's local braves originally supplemented where military strength was insufficient. Now the forces are sufficient for the task; order them disbanded and sent back to farming.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stated: "The local braves under Changxi were originally raised to make up for insufficient regular forces. Now the army is strong enough; order them disbanded and sent back to their farms."

sentences.zh: 」命昶熙回京供職。

translations.literal: " Changxi was ordered to return to the capital to resume his duties.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi was ordered to return to the capital and resume his duties.

sentences.zh: 會陳大喜勾結苗練餘黨趨汝南，陷正陽、信陽、新蔡、息縣各民寨，乃暫留勦賊。

translations.literal: When Chen Daxi colluded with the remaining Miao militia and marched toward Runan, capturing civilian stockades at Zhengyang, Xinyang, Xincai, and Xixian, Changxi was temporarily kept on to suppress the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Daxi joined forces with remnants of Miao Peilin's militia and marched on Runan, seizing civilian stockades at Zhengyang, Xinyang, Xincai, and Xixian, Changxi was temporarily kept in the field to continue the campaign.

sentences.zh: 三年，進屯息縣，擒誅捻首趙國良、徐文田十餘名，盡复諸寨。

translations.literal: In the third year he advanced his garrison to Xixian, captured and executed the Nian chiefs Zhao Guoliang, Xu Wentian, and more than ten others, and fully recovered all the stockades.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he moved his headquarters to Xixian, captured and executed the Nian chiefs Zhao Guoliang, Xu Wentian, and more than ten others, and fully recovered all the stockades.

sentences.zh: 十一月，僧格林沁敗陳大喜、張總愚於光山，賊西竄，偪南陽。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month Sengge Rinchen defeated Chen Daxi and Zhang Zongyu at Guangshan; the bandits fled west and pressed on Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Sengge Rinchen defeated Chen Daxi and Zhang Zongyu at Guangshan. The rebels fled west and threatened Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 昶熙調張曜回屯唐縣，知府湯聘珍扼宛南。

translations.literal: Changxi ordered Zhang Yao back to garrison Tang County, and Prefect Tang Pinzhen held southern Wan.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi ordered Zhang Yao to return and garrison Tang County, while Prefect Tang Pinzhen blocked the southern approaches to Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 四年，僧格林沁戰歿曹州，諸軍並被譴，坐革職留任，詔回京。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Sengge Rinchen died in battle at Caozhou; all the armies were censured, and Changxi was punished by dismissal from rank while retained in post, then ordered back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Sengge Rinchen was killed in battle at Caozhou. All the commanders were censured; Changxi was stripped of rank but kept in office, and then ordered back to the capital.

sentences.zh: 六年，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢左都御史，兼署工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrently served as acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrently served as acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 時捻匪戡定，疏陳軍務漸平，宜益思寅畏，略曰：「功成而喜者，常人之同情；

translations.literal: At the time the Nian bandits had been pacified. He memorialized that military affairs were gradually calming and that one should think all the more of reverent caution, writing in summary: "Those who rejoice at success share ordinary human feeling;
translations.idiomatic: By then the Nian rebellion had been crushed. He memorialized that although military affairs were gradually settling, the court should be all the more mindful of reverent caution, writing in summary: "To rejoice at success is the common human response;

sentences.zh: 功成而懼者，聖人之遠慮。

translations.literal: those who fear at success embody the sage's far-sighted concern.
translations.idiomatic: to fear at success is the sage's far-sighted concern.

sentences.zh: 今日巨寇甫平，兵戈未息，滇、黔、秦、隴，烽火驚心；

translations.literal: Today the great bandits have just been pacified and the war is not yet ended: in Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi, and Gansu, beacon fires still alarm the heart;
translations.idiomatic: Great rebellions have only just been put down and war has not yet ended. In Yunnan, Guizhou, Shaanxi, and Gansu, beacon fires still strike fear;

sentences.zh: 皖、豫、直、東，瘡痍滿目。

translations.literal: in Anhui, Henan, Zhili, and Shandong, wounds fill the eye.
translations.idiomatic: in Anhui, Henan, Zhili, and Shandong, devastation meets the eye everywhere.

sentences.zh: 戡亂安民，一一尚煩宸慮，敬肆之機，間不容髮。

translations.literal: To pacify disorder and settle the people—each matter still taxes imperial concern; the moment for reverence or indulgence allows no interval.
translations.idiomatic: Pacifying chaos and restoring the people to peace still demands the Emperor's constant attention. The choice between reverence and complacency allows no delay.

sentences.zh: 萬一大捷之餘，偶忘乾惕，則患機之萌，恐有伏於無形者。

translations.literal: If, after a great victory, one briefly forgets vigilance, then the budding of misfortune may lurk unseen.
translations.idiomatic: If, in the wake of great victory, vigilance is briefly forgotten, disaster may already be forming out of sight.

sentences.zh: 今之所急：一在勤聖學。

translations.literal: What is urgent today: first, diligence in the Emperor's studies.
translations.idiomatic: What is urgent today: first, diligence in the Emperor's studies.

sentences.zh: 皇上春秋鼎盛，典學日新。

translations.literal: The Emperor is in the prime of youth, and his learning grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor is in the prime of youth, and his learning improves daily.

sentences.zh: 但恐親師講學，為時無多，還宮之後，左右近習，或以功業日盛，間進諛詞，意氣漸盈，懋修或懈。

translations.literal: But I fear the time spent with his tutors in lecture is not long, and after returning to the palace his close attendants, seeing achievements daily increase, may occasionally offer flattery; his spirit may gradually grow proud, and earnest self-cultivation may slacken.
translations.idiomatic: But I fear he spends too little time with his tutors. After returning to the palace, close attendants—seeing imperial achievements grow day by day—may offer flattery, his spirit may gradually swell with pride, and his earnest self-cultivation may slacken.

sentences.zh: 昔宋莊獻皇后臨朝，仁宗聽內侍之言，欲觀寶玩，莊獻太后為言祖宗創業之艱。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Empress Zhuangxian of Song held court, Emperor Renzong listened to inner attendants and wished to view precious curios; Empress Dowager Zhuangxian spoke to him of the hardship with which the ancestors had founded the enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: In Song times, when Empress Zhuangxian held court, Emperor Renzong listened to palace eunuchs and wished to view precious curios. Empress Dowager Zhuangxian reminded him of the hardships with which their ancestors had founded the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 臣亦伏原皇太后於皇上還宮之餘，殷殷以時事艱難，勤加啟迪。

translations.literal: Your servant also humbly hopes that, after the Emperor returns to the palace, the Empress Dowager will earnestly instruct him on the hardships of current affairs and diligently guide and enlighten him.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant also humbly hopes that after the Emperor returns to the palace, the Empress Dowager will earnestly remind him of the hardships of the times and guide him with constant care.

sentences.zh: 至於近侍，尤宜擇老成有識之人，服事起居，將見養正之功，日臻堅定矣。

translations.literal: As for close attendants, it is especially fitting to choose seasoned and knowledgeable men to serve in daily life; then the work of nurturing rectitude will daily grow firm.
translations.idiomatic: As for his close attendants, it is especially important to choose seasoned and thoughtful men to attend him in daily life. Then the work of nurturing his character will steadily take root.

sentences.zh: 一在崇節儉。

translations.literal: Second, uphold frugality.
translations.idiomatic: Second, uphold frugality.

sentences.zh: 今寇亂雖平，而流離之民，未盡歸農，荒蕪之田，尚多未墾。

translations.literal: Though bandit disorder is now pacified, displaced people have not all returned to farming, and many abandoned fields remain unreclaimed.
translations.idiomatic: Though rebellion has been put down, displaced people have not all returned to farming, and many fields still lie abandoned and unreclaimed.

sentences.zh: 非力加撙節，不足以廣積儲而備緩急。

translations.literal: Without forcefully applying thrift, it will not be enough to expand stores and prepare for emergencies.
translations.idiomatic: Without strict economy, the state cannot build up reserves or prepare for emergencies.

sentences.zh: 臣前管三庫事務，見內務府借撥部庫銀兩，逐歲加增。

translations.literal: Your servant previously managed affairs of the Three Treasuries and saw the Imperial Household Department borrow and allocate silver from the Ministry treasuries, increasing year by year.
translations.idiomatic: When your servant previously oversaw the Three Treasuries, he saw the Imperial Household Department borrow and draw silver from the Ministry treasuries in amounts that increased every year.

sentences.zh: 竊恐中原底定，踵事增華，財源未開，財流不節，度支告匱，為患匪輕。

translations.literal: I secretly fear that with the central plains settled, splendor will follow precedent and increase; revenue sources will not be opened, expenditure will not be restrained, the fiscal office will report shortage, and the harm will not be light.
translations.idiomatic: I fear that with the central plains now pacified, extravagance will follow old patterns: new revenue will not be developed, spending will not be restrained, the treasury will run short, and the consequences will be grave.

sentences.zh: 伏原皇太后、皇上崇尚節儉，為天下先。

translations.literal: I humbly hope the Empress Dowager and the Emperor will uphold frugality and take the lead for all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly hope the Empress Dowager and the Emperor will take the lead in practicing frugality for the whole empire.

sentences.zh: 一切不急之務，可罷則罷之，可緩則緩之，庶國用可充，而風俗亦漸歸質厚矣。

translations.literal: All non-urgent matters—what can be stopped, stop; what can be delayed, delay—so that state funds may be filled and customs may gradually return to plain sincerity.
translations.idiomatic: All non-urgent projects should be canceled where possible and postponed where they can wait, so that state funds may recover and public morals may gradually return to plain simplicity.

sentences.zh: 一在飭吏治。

translations.literal: Third, rectify official governance.
translations.idiomatic: Third, rectify official governance.

sentences.zh: 發、捻之禍，實由不肖州縣所激而成。

translations.literal: The calamities of the Miao and Nian rebellions were in truth stirred up by unworthy prefectural and county officials.
translations.idiomatic: The Miao and Nian rebellions were in truth provoked by unworthy prefectural and county officials.

sentences.zh: 正供之外，百計誅求；

translations.literal: Beyond regular taxes, they devised a hundred schemes of extortion;
translations.idiomatic: Beyond regular taxes, they devised every sort of extortion;

sentences.zh: 私派私罰，自營囊橐，以致民氣不伸，釀成巨患。

translations.literal: imposed private levies and private fines and filled their own purses, until popular grievances could find no outlet and a great calamity was brewed.
translations.idiomatic: imposed unauthorized levies and fines to fill their own pockets, until popular grievances had no outlet and a great disaster was brewed.

sentences.zh: 用兵以來，此風尤甚。

translations.literal: Since military campaigns began, this trend has been especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Since the wars began, this abuse has grown especially severe.

sentences.zh: 即如釐金一項，奉行不善，百弊叢生。

translations.literal: Take, for example, the likin tax: poorly implemented, a hundred abuses multiply.
translations.idiomatic: Take the likin transit tax, for example: poorly administered, it breeds a hundred abuses.

sentences.zh: 病商病民，莫此為甚。

translations.literal: Nothing harms merchants and people more than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing harms merchants and commoners more.

sentences.zh: 今日之封疆大吏，以地方多事，喜用精明強幹之員，而不求愷悌循良之吏。

translations.literal: Today's frontier great officials, because their regions have many affairs, prefer clever, capable, and forceful men and do not seek benevolent and orderly officials.
translations.idiomatic: Today's provincial governors, finding their regions still unsettled, prefer clever and forceful officials and do not seek humane and steady ones.

sentences.zh: 斯民元氣，剝削愈甚，其禍遂不可勝言。

translations.literal: The people's vital energy is stripped ever more severely, and the resulting calamity becomes unspeakable.
translations.idiomatic: The people's strength is drained ever further, and the harm becomes beyond reckoning.

sentences.zh: 今東南初定，畿甸甫清，兵燹遺黎，不堪再擾。

translations.literal: Now the southeast has just been settled and the capital region just cleared; the survivors of war cannot bear further disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: The southeast has only just been pacified and the capital region only just cleared. The war-weary people cannot endure further abuse.

sentences.zh: 應令各省督撫慎選良吏，與民休息，以復富庶之舊。

translations.literal: Each province's governor and governor-general should be ordered carefully to select good officials, give the people rest, and restore former prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Each province's governors and governor-generals should be ordered to choose good officials carefully, let the people recover, and restore former prosperity.

sentences.zh: 一在固根本。

translations.literal: Fourth, secure the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, secure the foundations of the realm.

sentences.zh: 陝西回逆、土匪，麕聚北山，現聞大軍乘勝西征，恐至窮而思竄。

translations.literal: Muslim rebels and bandits in Shaanxi gather like deer in the northern mountains. It is now heard that the great army is advancing west on the momentum of victory; I fear that when cornered they will seek to flee.
translations.idiomatic: Muslim rebels and bandits in Shaanxi are massing in the northern mountains. Now that the main army is advancing west on the momentum of victory, I fear that when cornered they will try to break out.

sentences.zh: 其或由晉省撲河，或由草地北擾宣、大，畿輔兵單地廣，在在須防。

translations.literal: They may either leap the Yellow River from Shanxi or, from the grasslands to the north, raid Xuan and Da. The capital region has few troops and broad territory—defense is needed everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: They may either cross the Yellow River from Shanxi or sweep north from the grasslands to raid Xuanhua and Datong. The capital region has too few troops for too vast a territory, and must be defended at every point.

sentences.zh: 直隸提督劉銘傳謀勇兼優，應令迅回本任，並帶所部萬人，留直屯守，以壯聲威。

translations.literal: Zhili regional commander Liu Mingchuan is superior in both planning and courage; he should be ordered quickly back to his original post, and to bring ten thousand men of his command to remain garrisoned in Zhili and strengthen prestige.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili regional commander Liu Mingchuan excels in both strategy and courage. He should be ordered back to his post at once, bring ten thousand of his troops to garrison Zhili, and strengthen the capital region's defenses.

sentences.zh: 並將綠營兵丁，練成勁旅，庶諸賊不敢萌心北擾，而諸將亦得專意西征矣。

translations.literal: And the Green Standard troops should be drilled into a crack force, so that the various bandits will not dare think of raiding north, and the generals may also devote themselves wholly to the western campaign.
translations.idiomatic: The Green Standard troops should also be drilled into a crack force, so that rebels will not dare think of raiding north and the generals can focus entirely on the western campaign.

sentences.zh: 」疏入，上嘉其言剴切，優詔答之。

translations.literal: When the memorial was submitted, the Emperor praised his words as incisive and answered with a special edict.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial reached the throne, the Emperor praised his blunt and forceful counsel and replied with a special commendation.

sentences.zh: 八年，授工部尚書，命在總理各國事務衙門行走。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Works and ordered to serve in the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of Works and assigned to the Zongli Yamen for foreign affairs.

sentences.zh: 九年，天津民、教構釁，命偕直隸總督曾國籓按治，暫署三口通商大臣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when civilians and missionaries clashed at Tianjin, he was ordered together with Zhili governor-general Zeng Guofan to investigate and settle the matter, and temporarily acted as commissioner for the three treaty ports.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when the Tianjin incident broke out between locals and missionaries, he was ordered to investigate jointly with Zhili governor-general Zeng Guofan and served temporarily as commissioner for the three treaty ports.

sentences.zh: 事定回京，請裁歸總督兼理，從之。

translations.literal: When the affair was settled he returned to the capital and asked that the post be abolished and returned to the governor-general's concurrent management; this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: After the affair was settled he returned to the capital and asked that the post be folded back under the governor-general; the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 十一年，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十二年，上謁東陵，命留京辦事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, when the Emperor visited the Eastern Tombs, Changxi was ordered to remain in the capital to handle affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, when the Emperor visited the Eastern Tombs, Changxi was ordered to remain in Beijing to handle affairs.

sentences.zh: 十三年，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he concurrently served as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was also appointed chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 光緒四年，丁母憂，服闋，命仍在總理各國事務衙門行走，兼翰林院掌院學士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Guangxu he entered mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was ordered still to serve in the Zongli Yamen and concurrently as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Guangxu he mourned his mother; when mourning ended he was ordered to continue at the Zongli Yamen while also serving as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy.

sentences.zh: 八年，授兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was appointed Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，優詔賜卹，贈太子少保，諡文達。

translations.literal: He soon died; a special edict granted mourning honors, posthumously promoted him to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous title Wenda.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died. The court issued a special edict granting mourning honors, posthumously promoted him to Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous title Wenda.

sentences.zh: 昶熙屢掌文衡，兩典會試，凡朝、殿考試，閱卷歷二十餘次，士論歸之。

translations.literal: Changxi repeatedly held literary examinations, twice presided over the metropolitan examination, and in palace and hall examinations graded papers more than twenty times; scholarly opinion looked to him.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi repeatedly oversaw the civil examinations, presided twice over the metropolitan examination, and graded papers in palace and hall examinations more than twenty times; scholars looked to him with respect.

sentences.zh: 論曰：袁甲三、毛昶熙並以謇諤著聲，出膺軍寄。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Yuan Jiasan and Mao Changxi both won renown for blunt integrity and were sent out to bear military responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators observe: Yuan Jiasan and Mao Changxi both won fame for blunt integrity and were sent out to bear military command.

sentences.zh: 甲三孤軍支拄淮壖，與捻事相終始，驕帥傾排，狡寇反覆，卒能保障岩疆，其堅毅不可及也。

translations.literal: Jiasan, with a lone army propping up the Huai frontier, was involved with the Nian affair from beginning to end; arrogant commanders plotted against him and cunning bandits turned treacherous again and again, yet in the end he could safeguard the strategic borderlands—his steadfastness was beyond reach.
translations.idiomatic: Jiasan held the Huai frontier alone with a scattered army, facing the Nian rebellion from start to finish. Arrogant commanders undermined him and cunning rebels turned treacherous again and again, yet he still safeguarded a critical frontier—his steadfastness was beyond compare.

sentences.zh: 昶熙事權未專，同時疆吏非辦賊才，補苴之功，亦不可沒。

translations.literal: Changxi never held sole authority, and the frontier officials of his day were not men fit to suppress bandits; yet his work of patching and holding things together should not be forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: Changxi never held full authority, and many frontier officials of his day were not equal to suppressing bandits; yet his work of holding things together should not be forgotten.

sentences.zh: 所陳平捻方略，具得要領。

translations.literal: The strategy he set forth for pacifying the Nian grasped the essentials.
translations.idiomatic: The strategy he laid out for pacifying the Nian hit the essentials.

sentences.zh: 賊平之後，懃懃以寅畏納諫，老成謀國，於斯見之。

translations.literal: After the bandits were pacified, he earnestly urged reverent caution and acceptance of counsel; his statesmanlike concern for the realm is seen in this.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, he earnestly urged reverent caution and openness to counsel—a seasoned statesman's care for the realm shows in this.

sentences.zh: 保恆濟美戎行，立朝侃侃，家英國幹，鬱有風規已。

translations.literal: Bao Heng carried on his father's military merit, spoke forthrightly at court, and came from a family of national talent; he already bore a noble reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Bao Heng inherited his father's military distinction, spoke forthrightly at court, and came from a family of national talent; even early on he bore a reputation for integrity and ability.
